commits.pr_title: [Attention] Decode FlashInfer spec queries with fa2 on pre-SM90 GPUs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On pre-SM90 GPUs FlashInfer has no XQA or trtllm-gen decode, so speculative decoding verification steps (1 + `num_speculative_tokens` tokens per request) are split off as prefills, and `get_cudagraph_support` reports `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE`, which drops spec decode from `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` to `PIECEWISE`. FlashInfer's fa2 tensor-core decode already takes uniform multi-token queries (`q_len_per_req`) and keeps them CUDA-graph safe ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3871](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3871), in 0.7.0.post1), so this sends uniform verification queries through it and reports `UNIFORM_BATCH` there.

## Claims

- On pre-SM90 GPUs, FlashInfer spec decode runs its verification steps in full CUDA graphs. On SM80 with Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 and MTP (3 tokens), decode goes from 73.6 to 108.1 tok/s at TP=1 and from 61.0 to 83.1 tok/s at TP=2, with the same greedy output.
- Without speculative decoding nothing changes: same throughput, same tokens and the same KV cache size.
- SM90 and later keep their decode selection and graph support; single-token native decode is planned exactly as before.

## Validation

`test_flashinfer_fa2_spec_decode_correctness` (new, runs on pre-SM90 GPUs and skips elsewhere) checks uniform 4-token queries over three requests against SDPA, eager and under CUDA graph replay, and that the decode was planned with `q_len_per_req=4`. The test harness's `num_speculative_tokens` option built its speculative config as a `SimpleNamespace` that lacks fields the builders now read, so it fails for FlashInfer on every GPU; it now builds a real `SpeculativeConfig`. `test_flashinfer_varlen_cudagraph_capability` mocks a trtllm-gen platform and now also pins the device capability, since the varlen bound is `None` on pre-SM90 GPUs.

Everything below ran on SM80 with the FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 release wheel that vLLM pins, installed apart from any source build. `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -k "flashinfer or FLASHINFER"` gives 149 passed, 53 skipped on this PR and 147 passed, 53 skipped on `main` (`32fbfa15e8`); the two new cases are the difference.

End to end, `main` (`32fbfa15e8`) against `main` + this PR: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 weights, NVFP4 KV cache, FlashInfer, batch 1, default compile and CUDA graph settings, 256 greedy tokens, median of three runs after warm-up.

| | `main` | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TP=1, MTP with 3 tokens | 73.6 tok/s (`PIECEWISE`) | 108.1 tok/s (decode `FULL`) |
| TP=1, no spec decode | 57.2 tok/s | 57.5 tok/s |
| TP=2, MTP with 3 tokens | 61.0 tok/s (`PIECEWISE`) | 83.1 tok/s (decode `FULL`) |
| TP=2, no spec decode | 59.0 tok/s | 59.0 tok/s |

Output tokens are identical between the two builds in every row, and MTP accepts the same drafts (684 of 1032 at TP=1, 668 of 1092 at TP=2). KV cache size is unchanged without spec decode and about 0.05 GiB smaller with MTP, which now captures FULL decode graphs.

## Details

- Spec queries count as decodes on pre-SM90 GPUs (`supports_spec_as_decode`), so the reorder threshold becomes 1 + `num_speculative_tokens`. DCP still forces it back to 1.
- `get_cudagraph_support` returns `UNIFORM_BATCH` on pre-SM90 GPUs. DCP and non-causal draft attention stay at `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE`, and `get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len` returns `None` there since fa2 has no varlen decode.
- The native decode branch already gets only uniform decodes (`require_uniform=True` sends mixed lengths to prefill). With more than one token per request it plans the wrapper per request with `q_len_per_req`; FULL uniform-decode graphs are captured only up to `max_num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` tokens, so there the token count is exactly requests × query length. Single-token decode keeps planning by token count.
- FlashInfer freezes a CUDA-graph decode wrapper to its batch size and query length, so the wrapper cache is keyed by both.

An earlier attempt ([#50885](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50885)) targeted SM12x and was closed once XQA covered that architecture; it did not cover pre-SM90.

---

commits.pr_title: [Refactor] Migrate FlashInfer NVLink one-sided to MoEEpCommunication
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Migrate `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` from the deprecated `MoeAlltoAll` entry point to FlashInfer's `MoEEpCommunication` API introduced in [FlashInfer #5532](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5532).

This is an API prerequisite for the CFT integration discussed in [#57069](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57069). It does not enable CFT or migrate the two-sided backend.

FlashInfer 0.7.2 is released and upstream's stable dependency update is merged. Head `a0d97611` also addresses the public-API compatibility feedback: prefer checkpoint methods on `communication`, retain the 0.7.2 `.alltoall` fallback, and avoid importing removed legacy cache classes during test teardown. **The updated source passed all 11 one/two-sided tests on 0.7.2 and all 9 one-sided tests on the pinned upcoming FlashInfer API, with zero skips.**

## Claims

- Adopt `create_communication`, typed dispatch results, and the communication wrapper's combine interface.
- Preserve dispatch workspace sizing for BF16/FP16, NVFP4, MXFP8, and DeepSeek blockwise FP8, including padded MXFP8 scales.
- Share one communication wrapper across layers, growing token, dispatch, and combine capacities independently.
- Preserve the existing low-precision combine option and keep bootstrap metadata on CPU when CUDA is the default device.
- Extend regression coverage for workspace growth, quantized payloads, empty ranks, CUDA Graph replay, and low-precision combine.

## Validation

### Latest head — stable and upcoming API compatibility (October 19, 2026)

Head `a0d97611`, job **804205**, one exclusive Rubin node (`hecate0004`), pinned CUDA 13.4 image; **COMPLETED 0:0**.

| Dependency / check | Result |
|---|---|
| Official FlashInfer 0.7.2: one-sided + two-sided | 11/11 passed (9 one-sided, 2 two-sided), zero skips |
| FlashInfer [#6621](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6621) at `aa7ad45a32a6a5bf25b77803ff5afa3c66204cc1`: one-sided | 9/9 passed, zero skips |
| Actual-module import and manager checkpoint API-selection checks, both variants | Passed |
| Pre-commit, mypy and commit hooks | Passed |
| GPU cleanup / memory-clock reset | Passed; no GPU processes remained |

The existing GPU tests exercise checkpoint/restore and subsequent eager/CUDA Graph execution, empty ranks, workspace growth, quantized payloads and worker shutdown. The newer dependency has both legacy modules removed; its import checks confirm the public checkpoint API is selected. The shared `CustomCommunicator` no longer requires the legacy two-sided backend to exist. Legacy cache cleanup accesses only classes already loaded in the process.

The newer dependency is **unreleased source**, not a stable release. Its pinned source includes the upstream SM107 JIT build fix. This validates the one-sided path with the upcoming API; the production two-sided migration remains a separate change. The stable run retains a shared-memory resource-tracker warning, with no test failures or native shutdown crashes.

Commands: `python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py -k 'one_sided or two_sided' -v -s --timeout=1200` on 0.7.2; the same command with `-k one_sided` on the newer source. Both use fresh processes and separate JIT caches. No dispatch/combine implementation or numerical tolerances changed. Full model evaluations below were not repeated on the new FlashInfer revision.

### Previous head — two-sided shutdown fix (October 18, 2026)

Head `5d917258` was checked with FlashInfer **0.7.2 stable** and the pinned CUDA 13.4 image on Rubin GPUs in job `798176`. The committed source was verified to match the tested candidate.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Two-sided communication, repetition 1 | 2/2 passed, zero skips, exit 0 |
| Two-sided communication, repetition 2 | 2/2 passed, zero skips, exit 0 |
| Two-sided communication, repetition 3 | 2/2 passed, zero skips, exit 0 |
| One-sided communication | 9/9 passed, zero skips, exit 0 |
| Changed-file pre-commit hooks, including mypy | Passed |
| Post-test GPU cleanup and memory-clock reset | Passed |

The fix adds explicit cleanup of FlashInfer's cached two-sided workspace tensor views and their owners at the end of the test worker, before interpreter finalization. Child exit-code assertions remain enabled. This is a test-only shutdown fix; it does not change production communication or kernels.

The same allocation also ran an unmodified `36b34b68` control, which reproduced both shutdown SIGSEGVs. The diagnostic job deliberately preserves those control failures and therefore has aggregate Slurm status **FAILED 1:0**; **all candidate tests passed**. This resolves the observed test shutdown failure in this environment, without claiming a general production lifecycle fix.

### Stable model and component validation — October 18, 2026

Baseline `e80b6c64` and migrated `f592f3b5` used FlashInfer **0.7.2 stable**, the same pinned CUDA 13.4 image, and Rubin GPUs (job `796374`).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Dispatch layout | 13 passed, zero skips |
| One-sided communication | 9 passed, zero skips |
| MoE layer, DP=EP=2 and 4 / TP=1 | Three subcases per topology passed: two BF16 configurations and blocked FP8 |
| Fixed model prompts, eager and Graph | 24/24 exact token and logprob matches between baseline and migration in each mode |
| Full GSM8K, eager | 89.69% baseline → 89.08% migrated |
| Full GSM8K, Graph | 89.54% baseline → 89.69% migrated |
| Historical two-sided controls, before the test cleanup fix | Both baseline and migration reproduced shutdown SIGSEGVs; superseded for current-head test status by the passing results above |

Model evaluation used Qwen3-30B-A3B, 1,319 GSM8K questions, five-shot prompting and max 256 output tokens. Mixed prefill/decode and actual CUDA Graph replay were checked. All model-comparison gates passed; no accuracy or performance improvement is claimed.

The layer-log parser initially misclassified inline `PASSED` as missing because it required a preceding newline. Each named subcase and the “3 passed of 3 total subcases” summaries were reconciled against the raw logs. The original logs and failed job status remain preserved: the two-sided native crashes are real failures, and the overall job is **FAILED 1:0**, not a clean pass.

The intermediate `36b34b68` rerun (job `798024`) passed 9/9 one-sided tests but still reproduced the two-sided shutdown failure. These historical failures are retained in the evidence; the current-head results above supersede them. At `36b34b68` and `5d917258`, production code was identical to `f592f3b5`. The October 19 follow-up changes checkpoint API selection and the shared communicator's import dependency; its targeted cross-version validation is listed above.

All eight changed files at `f592f3b5` passed pre-commit, including mypy; the changed test file at `36b34b68` also passed all applicable hooks. The official stable wheel’s corresponding 499 MoE EP / one-sided Python files match the stable tag; these API paths are unchanged from the official rc3 tag.

Preparation job `796345` ran no tests because source verification followed a Git symlink to a directory. Symlink-target hashing was corrected in the separate `796374` attempt; original evidence was retained.

### Previous validation — October 14, 2026

Migration commit `c1ad8076` was validated against vLLM baseline `5555a2d8` using FlashInfer **0.7.2rc3**, CUDA **13.4**, and two Rubin GPUs. Baseline and migrated code used the same dependency versions.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Changed-file pre-commit hooks, including mypy | Passed |
| Host manager lifecycle/capacity checks | 28 passed; GPU allocation and collectives stubbed |
| Dispatch layout tests | 13 passed, zero skips |
| One-sided GPU communication tests | 9 passed, zero skips |
| MoE layer regression, DP=EP=2 / TP=1 | BF16 and blocked-FP8 cases passed, zero skips |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B, eager and CUDA Graph | Model comparison checks passed |

For each execution mode, baseline and migrated code produced **identical token sequences and logprobs for all 24 fixed prompts**. Validation also exercised mixed prefill/decode traffic, verified actual CUDA Graph replay, and enabled `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

Full GSM8K evaluation used 1,319 questions, five-shot prompting, and a maximum of 256 output tokens:

| Execution mode | Baseline accuracy | Migrated accuracy |
|---|---:|---:|
| Eager | 89.16% | 90.07% |
| CUDA Graph | 89.76% | 90.22% |

These results support correctness; no accuracy improvement or performance improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Historical two-sided shutdown failures — resolved in the current test run</summary>

Both two-sided regression tests encountered child-process `SIGSEGV` during interpreter teardown, with a tensor/storage-deleter stack under `Py_FinalizeEx`.

The **unchanged baseline reproduced both failures under the same dependency versions**. This supports treating the issue as existing in the tested environment rather than specific to this migration. The failures remain recorded as failures; the overall validation job retained a nonzero exit status.

The distributed test launcher checks child exit codes so native crashes cannot silently appear as passing tests. The explicit end-of-worker cleanup in `5d917258` resolves this failure in the tested environment, as shown by the same-allocation control/candidate experiment above.

</details>

### Component test commands

```bash
python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  -k one_sided -v

python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py \
  -k 'one_sided or two_sided' -v -s
```

AI assistance was used to prepare the implementation and tests.

commits.pr_title: [Model] NemotronHMTP: share the target's embedding and LM head
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`NemotronHMTP` now loads only `mtp.*` weights and always uses the target's embedding and LM head, on every pipeline stage. Both modules start as `None`, and `has_own_embed_tokens = False` / `has_own_lm_head = False` let the existing sharing helpers attach the target's modules before execution. Because the drafter holds the target's modules, a target weight refit also updates the drafter.

Before this change, with PP=2 the drafter got its own copy of the embedding instead of the target's. MTP acceptance dropped to about 9%.

This is a self-contained split of #62017 by @aoshen02, with authorship retained.

## Behavior change

On main, a checkpoint containing `lm_head.*` sets `has_own_lm_head = True`, and the drafter shares the head only if it equals the target's. With this PR the drafter always uses the target's head. For Nemotron-H checkpoints the MTP `lm_head.*` is the target's, so the result is the same. A checkpoint with a genuinely different MTP head would have that head ignored.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py
```

The new tests check two things:
- Only `mtp.*` weights are loaded, with and without the `language_model.` prefix.
- With PP=1 and PP=2 the drafter shares the target embedding, and a target refit is visible to the drafter.

Model probe: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`, GH200, TP=1, MTP with 3 draft tokens, temperature 0, 12 prompts × 64 tokens, eager.

## Test Result

- Both test files: 45 passed.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passes on the changed files.

| Run | Embedding / head shared | Draft acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PP=2, main | head only | 161/1797 (9.0%) |
| PP=2, this PR | both | 526/747 (70.4%) |
| PP=1, this PR | both | 526/747 (70.4%) |

With this PR, the PP=1 and PP=2 outputs are token-identical on 12/12 prompts.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Download quick-reduce e2e model when cached snapshot has no weights
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

`test_quick_allreduce_llm_e2e` and `test_quick_allreduce_llm_e2e_ray` in `tests/distributed/test_rocm_quick_reduce.py` fail in `(MI300) Distributed Features` because the engine cannot start: `RuntimeError: Cannot find any model weights with /home/buildkite-agent/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct/snapshots/7ae55760...`.

Failure: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15208/list?jid=01a1636b-f116-4ace-b3ca-bdae8a9f5e55&tab=output

## Cause

No recent commit changed this test. `_get_model_path()` was added in #40990 and returns the local snapshot whenever `snapshot_download(local_files_only=True)` succeeds. If only the config and tokenizer are in the HF cache (for example, after another test fetched them with `hf_hub_download`), `huggingface_hub` has no cached file listing for the repo, so it cannot tell that the snapshot is incomplete and returns the folder without weights. Whether the test passes depends on the node's cache. The previous nightly passed on a node whose cache had the weights, with the same snapshot path.

## Fix

Use the cached snapshot only if it contains `*.safetensors`. Otherwise fall back to the existing download path.

## Test plan

On MI300X, with an HF cache holding only the config and tokenizer files for `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, so that the old code returns a snapshot without weights: `pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_rocm_quick_reduce.py -k "test_quick_allreduce_llm_e2e and not ray"` downloads the snapshot and passes.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Gemma4][Multimodal] Fuse Gemma4Unified 2D posemb and batch image/video embedder
commits.pr_body:
## Overview This pull request optimizes the vision and multimodal input processing pipeline of `Gemma4Unified` (`vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py`, used by `google/gemma-4-12B-it`) via two key performance and architectural enhancements: 1. **Vectorized PyTorch 2D Factorized Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: Replaces the sequential, un-fused PyTorch loop over coordinate axes and position indices with a single clean, vectorized PyTorch implementation using contiguous 1D `F.embedding` lookups on `self.pos_embedding.view(-1, embed_dim)`, in-place `.add_` accumulation, and masked fill, cleanly preserving `positions_xy != -1` coordinate masking with 100% bit-exact numerical parity without requiring Triton or custom C++/CUDA kernels. 2. **Memory-Bounded Chunking & Cross-Request Image & Multi-Frame Video Batching**: Vectorizes `_process_image_input` (both 3D `torch.Tensor` and `list[torch.Tensor]`) and `_process_video_input` across all prompt requests and video frames into unified 2D batch GEMM projections (`self.patch_dense` and `self.embed_vision`), eliminating per-request and per-frame Python iteration overhead. Memory usage is safely bounded via `_vision_chunk` which dynamically mirrors `_encoder_chunk` logic and bounds peak memory per chunk based on available accelerator memory (short-circuiting memory queries when batch size <= 1, and guarded with `gpu_sync_allowed()`). Duplicate-work check: verified via GitHub PR search that no open pull request vectorizes the Gemma 4 Unified 2D position embedding or batches its multimodal vision embedder projections. ## Claims 1. **Component Vision & Video Embedder Speedup (`Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`, `google/gemma-4-12B-it`)**: - **Vectorized Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: **1.25x – 1.38x speedup** (`0.310 ms -> 0.248 ms` at 280 tokens; `0.325 ms -> 0.236 ms` at 2240 tokens) with **100.0% bit-exact parity**. - **Batched Image Input Processing (`_process_image_input`)**: - `1 image` (`280` patches): **1.23x speedup** (`1.413 ms -> 1.148 ms`, **100.0% bit-exact**). - `2 images` (`560` patches): **2.03x speedup** (`2.648 ms -> 1.306 ms`, `-1.34 ms`). - `4 images` (`1120` patches): **2.71x speedup** (`4.714 ms -> 1.743 ms`, `-2.97 ms`). - `8 images` (`2240` patches): **3.30x speedup** (`9.030 ms -> 2.737 ms`, `-6.29 ms`). - `16 images` (`4480` patches): **4.28x speedup** (`18.125 ms -> 4.234 ms`, `-13.89 ms`). - Variable-length image batches (`list[torch.Tensor]`): up to **4.46x speedup** (`9.572 ms -> 2.147 ms` at 8 images). - **Batched Video Input Processing (`_process_video_input`)**: - `1 video (4 frames)`: **3.92x speedup** (`5.100 ms -> 1.302 ms`, `-3.80 ms`). - `1 video (8 frames)`: **5.47x speedup** (`9.600 ms -> 1.754 ms`, `-7.85 ms`). - `2 videos (16 frames)`: **6.32x speedup** (`18.215 ms -> 2.883 ms`, `-15.33 ms`). - `4 videos (32 frames)`: **6.82x speedup** (`37.385 ms -> 5.480 ms`, `-31.91 ms`). - `8 videos (64 frames, Suite 1)`: **6.94x speedup** (`73.23 ms -> 10.56 ms`, `-62.67 ms`). 2. **Realistic End-to-End Serving Impact (Amdahl's Law on Encoder-Free `Gemma4Unified`)**: - Because `Gemma4Unified` (`google/gemma-4-12B-it`) is an **encoder-free** architecture (its vision module is only 2 linear projections + 3 norms + 2D pos lookup, with no ViT tower), GPU vision embedding takes `1.22–35.79 ms` for `1–32` images vs `70–1030 ms` for CPU PIL image preprocessing + the 40-layer 12B language model inside `llm.generate()`. - Benchmarked on the V1 engine with `enforce_eager=False` (`torch.compile` + CUDA Graphs enabled), the deterministic GPU vision embedder savings (`-0.11 ms` at 1 image up to `-13.55 ms` at 16 images and `-62.67 ms` at 64 video frames) translates to a **1.01x – 1.04x end-to-end `llm.generate()` speedup** (`72.69 -> 70.43 ms` prefill at `bs=1`, `408.97 -> 393.92 ms` prefill at `bs=8`, `1076.41 -> 1031.63 ms` E2E at `bs=8`) with **100.0% greedy token parity**. 3. **Strict Architectural Isolation**: - All changes are strictly isolated to `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py` (`Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`, used exclusively by `google/gemma-4-12B-it`). Tower-based Gemma 4 models (`E2B`, `E4B`, `26B-A4B`, `31B`) use `gemma4_mm.py` and are 100% untouched. 4. **Lossless Numerical & Bit-Level Parity**: - **100.0% Bit-Exact** on factorized 2D position embeddings (`bit_exact_pct = 100.0%`, `within_1ulp_pct = 100.0%`, `max_abs_diff = 0.0`, `cosine_sim = 1.00000`). - Bit-exact on small image batches, and `>= 0.99999` cosine similarity across large multi-image and multi-frame video batches (standard BF16 GEMM batching associativity). ## Validation ### 1. Unit Tests & Linters All linters and unit tests pass cleanly with 0 errors: ```bash # Unit test suite pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py # Output: 20 passed, 19 skipped # Ruff linter ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py # Output: All checks passed! # Ruff formatter ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py # Output: 2 files already formatted # Standalone microbenchmark verification python performance-speedup/pr_benchmarks/bench_pr4_unified_vision.py --mode standalone # Output: All 16 benchmark cases executed successfully with 0 parity errors ``` ### 2. Component Microbenchmark Timings & Numerical Parity (A100-SXM4-80GB Measured) Cross-branch comparison between `main` (`0838cd6593`) and feature branch (`lucianommartins/gemma4-pr4-unified-vision`) on NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB: | Benchmark Case | Baseline (ms) | Feature (ms) | Speedup | Gain (%) | Bit-Exact (%) | Within 1-ULP (%) | Max Diff | Cos Sim | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb (tokens=280) | 0.310 | 0.248 | **1.25x** | +25.2% | 100.0% | 100.0% | 0.0 | 1.00000 | | Technical Details ### Root Cause Analysis In `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` (`vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py`): 1. **Un-vectorized 2D Position Embedding Kernel**: `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb` previously computed factorized 2D sinusoidal position embeddings using separate PyTorch operations: slicing coordinate channels, executing multiple 3D tensor indexing lookups (`self.pos_embedding[clamped_pos[..., 0], 0, :]`), masking invalid patch positions where `positions_xy != -1`, and concatenating/normalizing. On modern GPUs, dispatching multiple small kernels over 280-2240 visual tokens caused excessive kernel launch latency (~0.31 ms), bounding vision preprocessing throughput. 2. **Sequential Un-batched Multimodal Inputs**: In `_process_image_input`, when multiple images were passed (either as a 3D tensor or a list of tensors across requests in continuous batching), each image was processed individually through `self.vision_embedder` and `self.embed_vision` via an inline `for pv, pp in zip(pixel_values, pixel_position_ids)` loop. Similarly, `_process_video_input` iterated over each video and each frame sequentially in Python. For an 8-frame video, this dispatched 8 independent vision embedder projections and 8 `ColumnParallelLinear` multimodal projections, incurring significant CPU launch overhead and leaving GPU SMs underutilized. ### Implementation Details 1. **Vectorized PyTorch 2D Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: - Replaces multi-step 3D tensor slicing with a single contiguous 1D embedding lookup using `F.embedding`. - Flattens `self.pos_embedding` from `[max_size, 2, embed_dim]` to `[max_size * 2, embed_dim]` via `.view(-1, embed_dim)`. - Computes flat indices `x_flat = pos_x * 2` and `y_flat = pos_y * 2 + 1`, clamping `-1` padding values before lookup. - Computes `out = F.embedding(x_flat, flat_weights)` and performs an in-place accumulation `out.add_(F.embedding(y_flat, flat_weights))`. - Applies `.masked_fill_(~valid_mask.unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)` in-place where `positions_xy == -1`, producing exact zero padding and preserving 100% bit-exact parity without Triton or custom kernel dependencies. 2. **Memory-Bounded Dynamic Chunking (`_vision_chunk` and `_embed_vision_patches`)**: - Mirrors the proven `_encoder_chunk` mechanism to dynamically split large image/video batches based on available accelerator memory budget, avoiding OOMs on large multimodal prompts. - Short-circuits when `total_items <= 1` (a single image or video), directly passing inputs through without executing the `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()` syscall. - Wraps accelerator memory queries with `with gpu_sync_allowed():` context guards to respect vLLM async execution and CUDA graph capture invariants. 3. **Unified Batched Multimodal Projections**: - `_process_image_input`: - When receiving a 3D `torch.Tensor` of shape `[N, S, D]` (batched images), it passes the tensor directly through `self._embed_vision_patches` in one pass, flattens all patches across images to `[N * S, D_in]`, executes a single batched GEMM projection through `self.embed_vision`, and unbinds into per-image feature chunks. - When receiving a `list[torch.Tensor]` of variable-length images, it flattens each image's patch tokens, tracks slice lengths, concatenates into a unified 2D batch `[total_patches, D]`, runs a single `self.embed_vision` projection, and splits back into per-image tensors using `torch.split`. - `_process_video_input`: - Embeds all frames of all videos in a single unified tensor pass through `self._embed_vision_patches` and `self.embed_vision`, splitting features by `video_frame_counts`. ### Tradeoffs & Encapsulation - **Zero Non-Gemma Regressions**: All modifications are strictly encapsulated within `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`. Standard Gemma 4 models (`E2B`, `E4B`, `26B-A4B`, `31B`) and text-only generation paths are completely untouched. - **Pure PyTorch Simplicity & Portability**: Completely eliminates the need for Triton or hardware-specific kernels, ensuring immediate zero-overhead support across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD ROCm, TPUs, and CPUs. - **Bit-Exact Numerical Fidelity**: Position embedding outputs are 100.0% bit-exact to PyTorch reference implementations. Full image and video embeddings retain 100.0% bit-exact parity at low batch sizes and > 0.99999 cosine similarity across large batches. ### Model & Workload Applicability Matrix | Model / Workload | Direct / Transitive / N/A | Supported Architecture | Technical Justification | | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | | `google/gemma-4-12B-it` | Direct Optimization | Gemma4Unified (Encoder-free Vision) | Uses `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`. | | `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. commits.pr_title: [Perf] Bypass DispatchPooler grouping for homogeneous tasks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
When all requests use the same pooling task, `DispatchPooler` still slices metadata and hidden states, calls the sub-pooler, and converts its dense output into individual row tensors. Bypass grouping for homogeneous tasks and return the sub-pooler's output directly, allowing MRv2's existing dense output path to issue one D2H copy for a fully finished batch.


## Claims
- Improve short-query embedding throughput by **3.8% at concurrency 64** and **10.3% at concurrency 128** on the GH200 workload below. The gain comes from doing less CPU work per request on the EngineCore busy loop, which is the bottleneck in this scenario: one batched device-to-host copy per step instead of one copy, one pinned-memory allocation and one pinned free (with their CUDA event bookkeeping) per request.
- Avoid redundant pooling metadata operations and per-row D2H copies when the sub-pooler returns a dense batch. Ragged outputs and the mixed-task fallback remain supported.


## Validation


### Benchmark

Embedding throughput for short text queries on one NVIDIA GH200 (144 GB). Each row is the mean of 2 server starts with 2 runs of 30 s each.

- **Model:** `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16` with online FP8 (`--quantization fp8_per_tensor`).
- **Data:** ViDoRe v3 finance (English) queries (mean length 31 tokens).
- **Server:** `--api-server-count 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, V2 model runner, `orjson` present.
- **Client:** concurrent `/v1/embeddings` requests from 8 client processes on a separate NUMA node.

| Concurrency | Metric | main | This PR | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | Throughput (req/s) | 4082 | 4236 | **+3.8%** |
| 64 | Latency p50 (ms) | 15.7 | 15.1 | −3.8% |
| 64 | Latency p99 (ms) | 16.5 | 16.1 | −2.0% |
| 128 | Throughput (req/s) | 6044 | 6665 | **+10.3%** |
| 128 | Latency p50 (ms) | 21.2 | 19.2 | −9.5% |
| 128 | Latency p99 (ms) | 22.6 | 21.6 | −4.3% |

Embeddings match main within its run-to-run variation: the minimum cosine similarity over 512 queries is **0.9996**, the same as the comparison between two main runs.

### Local checks

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_methods.py -q
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/special.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_methods.py
```

**58 tests passed**, covering dense and ragged sequence outputs, unfinished token-pooling state, and mixed-task token offsets. All pre-commit hooks passed.

## Details
The implementation adds a homogeneous-task check before the existing grouping loop. Returning the sub-pooler's output unchanged preserves dense tensors instead of splitting them into Python row objects. Sub-poolers can still return ragged lists, including for requests with different embedding dimensions or token counts. Mixed tasks, empty batches, and unsupported tasks retain the existing fallback behavior.

Frontend pooling multi-task support was deprecated in #37956 and removed in #37861. Instances select one pooling task through `PoolerConfig(task=...)`, making homogeneous batches the normal frontend path even when a model supports multiple selectable tasks.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] Use the sorted fused-MoE path for host-resident expert weights
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

At small batch (`num_tokens * top_k * 4 <= num_experts`, e.g. up to 4 tokens for Qwen3 MoE) the Triton fused-MoE path skips `moe_align_block_size` and gives every (token, expert) pair its own block (#29354, #39016). That saves the alignment kernel when weights are in device memory. With UVA weight offloading (`--offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-params experts`) the expert weights are read from host memory in place, and an expert routed to several tokens is then read over PCIe once per token. This PR takes the sorted path when the expert weights carry the UVA offload marker, so each routed expert is read once per step. Device-resident weights keep the naive path.

## Claims

On RTX 4090 (PCIe 4.0 x16), natural-text chat requests, 128 output tokens:

- Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8, one GPU, 16 GiB of experts offloaded: **+7% / +10% / +15–19% output throughput at 2 / 3 / 4 requests in flight**; unchanged at 1, 8 and 16.
- Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8, TP8, 16 GiB per GPU offloaded: **+7% / +10% / +18% at 2 / 3 / 4**; unchanged at 1.
- Base is the vLLM 0.31.0 wheel, whose two touched files are byte-identical to the base commit. Measured on CUDA only; ROCm's Triton path takes the same branch.
- No change without offloading: the code path is the same; measured on the 30B at TP2 with weights in VRAM (one start per build).
- Quality: GSM8K (lm-eval 0.4.13, 5-shot, greedy, first 250 questions, 4 requests in flight so decode steps take the changed path), 30B with 16 GiB offloaded: 0.888 flexible / 0.880 strict exact match for both builds, and all 250 responses byte-identical.
- Output: greedy completions identical to unpatched on the 30B (all starts). On the 235B at TP8 greedy output varies from start to start *without* the patch (three unpatched starts gave three different completions and three patched starts two, with one completion common to both builds), so it cannot distinguish the builds there.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k "host_resident_weights or naive_block_assignment"`: 44 passed on an RTX 4090, on the original base and again after rebasing onto current main (nightly wheel of the base commit, patched files applied). The new `test_host_resident_weights_take_sorted_path` runs UVA-mapped weights (and device weights as the control) at 1/2/4 tokens through both the modular `TritonExperts` path and the legacy `fused_moe`, asserts that `moe_align_block_size` is called exactly when the weights are host-resident, and compares the output with `torch_moe` (inputs scaled to O(1) outputs, `atol=rtol=2e-2`). Without the change its 6 host-resident cases fail.
- Every applicable pre-commit hook passes: ruff check/format, mypy 3.10–3.13, `check_torch_cuda`, test tethering, typos, SPDX, lazy imports, forbidden imports, boolean context manager.
- End to end, base vLLM against this PR, one `vllm serve`, requests from a client sending natural-language chat prompts (32 topics × 8 tasks, temperature 0.7, a fixed seed per request, `ignore_eos`):

  | setup | in flight | starts (base / PR) | output tok/s, base | output tok/s, this PR | change |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 30B, 1 GPU, 16 GiB on host | 1 | 2 / 2 | 20.7 | 20.5–20.7 | −0.5% (within spread) |
  | | 2 | 2 / 2 | 22.2 | 23.8 | +7% |
  | | 3 | 2 / 2 | 22.6 | 24.9–25.0 | +10% |
  | | 4 | 2 / 2 | 23.1 | 26.5–27.4 | +15–19% |
  | | 8 | 2 / 2 | 34.5–34.9 | 33.5–35.0 | within spread |
  | | 16 | 2 / 2 | 49.0–49.1 | 48.5–49.1 | within spread |
  | 235B, TP8, 16 GiB/GPU on host | 1 | 1 / 1 | 16.6 | 16.6 | 0% |
  | | 2 | 3 / 3 | 17.9–18.3 | 19.1–19.5 | +7% |
  | | 3 | 3 / 3 | 19.0 | 20.9 | +10% |
  | | 4 | 3 / 3 | 19.7 | 23.2–23.3 | +18% |
  | 30B, TP2, all in VRAM | 1–4 | 1 / 1 | 196.8 / 300.3 / 364.1 / 474.8 | 197.0 / 300.6 / 363.0 / 473.5 | within 0.3% |
  | | 8 | 1 / 1 | 741.5 | 727.1 | −1.9% (one start; both builds run the same code here) |

- Reproducible with vLLM's own benchmark (`vllm bench serve --dataset-name sharegpt --sharegpt-output-len 128 --ignore-eos --num-prompts N --max-concurrency c --seed 1`, ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split; N = 8 for c < 4, else 2c), 30B on one GPU with 16 GiB offloaded, two starts each:

  | `--max-concurrency` | output tok/s, base | output tok/s, this PR | change (midpoints) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 20.3 | 20.3 | 0% |
  | 2 | 21.3–22.2 | 23.4–23.6 | +8% |
  | 3 | 21.6–22.6 | 25.3–25.4 | +15% |
  | 4 | 22.2–23.0 | 25.6–26.7 | +16% |

<details>
<summary>Server commands</summary>

```
# 30B, one GPU (GPU 0 on NUMA node 3 here), 16 GiB of experts on the host
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 numactl --cpunodebind=3 --membind=3 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 16 --cpu-offload-params experts
# 235B, TP8
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --offload-backend uva --cpu-offload-gb 16 --cpu-offload-params experts --kv-cache-dtype fp8
```
The table above the benchmark used our own client sending natural-language chat prompts (32 topics × 8 tasks, temperature 0.7, fixed seed per request, 128 tokens with `ignore_eos`; N requests at concurrency c, N = 8 for c < 4, else 2c; one unrecorded warm-up per level).

</details>

## Details

**Why.** With experts in host memory, a decode step's cost is dominated by the bytes it reads over PCIe, and on the naive path an expert routed to several of the step's tokens is read once per token. The sorted path reads each routed expert once per step. How much that saves depends on how often a step's tokens share experts: on natural-text prompts the gain is in the Validation table; on random-token prompts with greedy decoding, whose routing is far more repetitive, the same change doubles throughput at 4 requests in flight. We report natural text.

**Implementation.**

- `_prepare_expert_assignment` takes `weights_host_resident` (default `False`), which disables the naive block assignment.
- `TritonExperts.apply` and the legacy `fused_experts_impl` pass `_weights_host_resident(w1, w2)`: true when either weight has `_vllm_is_uva_offloaded`, which the UVA offloader sets (and `device_loading_context` re-sets after `process_weights_after_loading`). `w1`/`w2` are the layer's own parameters on this path, so it is a getattr per forward inside the `moe_forward` custom op; the result depends only on the parameters, so CUDA-graph capture per size is unaffected. "Either", because UVA offloads per parameter and a budget cut-off can leave w13 on the host and w2 on the device.
- Other MoE paths are unaffected: Marlin and `TritonWNA16Experts` always align; the prefetch offloader copies weights to the device before compute and never sets the marker. Two model-specific callers of `_prepare_expert_assignment` (`models/k2_horizon.py`, `models/dots3_note/nvidia/vision_moe.py`) do not pass the flag and keep today's behaviour; they can opt in separately.
- Why a per-forward check rather than a decision when the kernel is built: `replace_parameter` in `process_weights_after_loading` installs a new Parameter without the marker, and `device_loading_context` re-marks it only afterwards, so a setup-time check would read False.

**Related.** No open or merged PR makes this change (searched 2026-10-07, rechecked 2026-10-16). The naive path came from #29354 and #39016; #34920 (closed, stale) proposed making it tunable from configs; #55268 (open) warms up Triton MoE variants per batch size, and this PR changes which variant host-resident weights use at ≤ 4 tokens. #57215 (open) keeps MoE experts offloaded during weight post-processing on XPU, the marker lifecycle this PR relies on; #56177 (open) is a shared GPU expert pool. RFC #38256 discusses expert caches for offloaded MoE, where a comment reports the same effect with a GPU-side slot buffer (the naive path stops sharing an expert's weight tile between tokens at batch ≥ 2). #37190, #57794 and #57943 decide which experts stay in VRAM; this PR is independent of that and helps whichever experts remain on the host.

**AI assistance.** Claude Opus 5.5 assisted with the code, tests, benchmarks and this description; the tests and benchmarks above were run on my hardware. I reviewed every changed line and the results, and can answer for it; the commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer.

commits.pr_title: [CPU] Warm up MRV2 Triton kernels at startup
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On x86 CPU the V2 model runner compiles its scheduler-driven Triton kernels (`input_batch`, `block_table`, the sampler, KV-block zeroing, ...) on first use, so the first requests after server start pay the compile in TTFT. With `triton-cpu` (installed by `requirements/cpu.txt` on `x86_64` since #58140) the first plain request waits ~11-20 s, and the first request using penalties or structured output waits 70-80 s.

Two changes:

- **Run `warmup_kernels` on CPU.** The GPU worker calls it from `compile_or_warm_up_model`, but `CPUWorker` overrides that method and never did. `profile_run` alone builds its tensors directly, so it never reaches these kernels.
- **Use `BLOCK_SIZE = 1024` on CPU for `_penalties_kernel` and `_apply_grammar_bitmask_kernel`.** 

## Test Plan

- End to end: Qwen3.5-9B, BF16, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`,  `--max-model-len 2048`, v0.32.0 CPU wheel with and without each change, cold Triton cache, AMD EPYC Turin (32 cores). Rounds of 2 concurrent streaming requests (512 input / 32 output tokens); rounds 2-4 each enable one sampler feature for the first time.
- Cold compile and steady-state runtime of the two bitmask kernels per block size (Qwen3.5 vocab, 248320), with OpenMP threads bound as in the CPU worker.

## Test Result

TTFT of the first request in each round (s), and engine init:

| build | engine init | plain | penalties | structured output | temperature / top-p / top-k | plain, steady | compiles in requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.32.0 | 84 s | 20.2 | 81.0 | 73.7 | 11.0 | 1.7 | 32 |
| + `warmup_kernels` only | 317 s | 4.3 | 1.7 | 2.5 | 1.7 | 1.7 | 2 |
| + this PR | 100 s | 3.9 | 1.7 | 2.5 | 1.7 | 1.7 | 2 |

Bitmask kernels, cold compile per kernel and runtime at 64 tokens:

| BLOCK_SIZE | `_penalties_kernel` compile | `_apply_grammar_bitmask_kernel` compile | LLVM IR | penalties runtime | bitmask runtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.7 s | 1.4 s | 0.8 MB | 403 µs | 102 µs |
| 2048 | 2.4 s | 2.1 s | 3.0 MB | 400 µs | 99 µs |
| 8192 | 71.0 s | 70.5 s | 47.9 MB | 764 µs | 151 µs |

commits.pr_title: [CPU][GDN] Route FP16 attention through Triton/FLA
commits.pr_body:
Keep BF16 on the optimized C++ kernels while allowing FP16 models to use the supported Triton/FLA fallback path.



## Overview

CPU GDN attention rejects FP16 before any kernel runs (`CPU GDN attention requires BF16`). Route FP16 through the existing Triton/FLA path in `layer._forward_core`, and leave BF16 on the C++ kernels.

## Claims

- FP16 CPU GDN (Qwen3.5 gated-delta) completes instead of dying on the BF16 assert.
- BF16 still uses `cpu_gdn_attention_core` and the packed C++ conv / chunk kernels.
- FP16 accuracy was measured on the full GSM8K test set: **0.9083** exact match for both strict-match and flexible-extract.

## Validation

Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, `dtype=float16`, GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy (`max_gen_toks=2048`), `max_model_len=4096`, `language_model_only`, `enable_thinking=False`, `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype=auto`. Triton wheel `3.8.0+cpu`. vLLM `v0.30.1rc1.dev727+g331382598`. All 1319 problems finished.

| Filter | Metric | Score |
| --- | --- | --- |
| flexible-extract | exact_match | 0.9083 ± 0.008 |
| strict-match | exact_match | 0.9083 ± 0.008 |

The two filters agree, and the first sample is a normal solution ending in `#### 18`. Without this branch the same launch asserts in `cpu_gdn_attention_core` and never scores.

```bash
VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=400 TRITON_PRINT_AUTOTUNING=1 lm_eval \
  --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B,dtype=float16,max_model_len=4096,language_model_only=True,enable_thinking=False,trust_remote_code=True,mamba_ssm_cache_dtype=auto \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --batch_size auto \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048 \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --output_path accuracy-dir \
  --log_samples
```

CPU GDN FP16 with this checkpoint is not in CI. The run above is the validation.

## Details

`QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention.forward_cpu` always calls `cpu_gdn_attention_core`. That op asserts `mixed_qkv.dtype == torch.bfloat16`, so `dtype=float16` (which casts the BF16 checkpoint to FP16) never reaches a kernel. The C++ conv and chunk kernels are BF16 implementations; opening them to FP16 is a separate change.

The FP16 branch calls `layer._forward_core` and returns. On CPU that path already uses PyTorch conv and the FLA chunk and decode kernels, which accept FP16. BF16 falls through to the existing assert and the C++ nonspec / spec paths. The branch sits in front of the spec-cache split, so FP16 spec-decode also takes `_forward_core`. The GSM8K run was non-speculative (`speculative_config=None`).

A cold Triton autotune on the first prefill can exceed the default 300s `execute_model` timeout. The scored run got past that and then ran normally.

---

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add Alpamayo 2 Super (reasoning model)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add `nvidia/Alpamayo2-Super`. vLLM serves its Qwen3-VL reasoning model, which produces all of the model's text outputs: VQA, grounding, chain-of-causation reasoning with meta-actions, and auto-labeling. The trajectory expert stored in the same checkpoint is not loaded. This follows `Cosmos3ForConditionalGeneration`. The full policy (reasoning + trajectory) will be served by vLLM-Omni (vllm-project/vllm-omni#9133).

## Claims

- `vllm serve nvidia/Alpamayo2-Super` works on the released checkpoint as-is: no conversion and no extra flags. The checkpoint's architecture `Alpamayo2Super` resolves to `Alpamayo2SuperForConditionalGeneration`.
- Matches the reference implementation ([NVlabs/alpamayo2](https://github.com/NVlabs/alpamayo2) @ `9596749e`):
  - token-identical prompts;
  - LingoQA 80.8% vs the reference's 81.0% (Lingo-Judge, 500 questions; model card: 79.2);
  - no throughput or latency cost against the same weights served as plain Qwen3-VL.
- Prompts can carry the model's ego-trajectory and special tokens as text. The new `alpamayo2_super` tokenizer mode is selected automatically and adds them with the reference ids.

## Validation

Environment: 1x H200 NVL, using `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` built from `8e2beaa3b` with this branch's `vllm/` diff applied.

**Serving the released checkpoint**

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Alpamayo2-Super --max-model-len 16384 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 24}'
```

The log shows `Resolved architecture: Alpamayo2Super` and `Defaulting to tokenizer_mode='alpamayo2_super'`. The model takes 62.5 GiB (bf16, expert skipped).

**Parity with the reference implementation**

The test set is 3 validation samples × 5 requests: 2 VQA questions, grounding, meta-action, and auto-labeling. All requests are greedy with 6 cameras × 4 frames, about 4.5k prompt tokens each, and the server runs with `--no-enable-prefix-caching` so its greedy output is reproducible. Prompts are built as in the reference `text_tasks.build_text_task_messages` and sent through `/v1/chat/completions`. The reference ran 4 times, once with float and once with uint8 image inputs each time.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| prompt token ids identical to the reference (incl. history/future trajectory tokens) | 15/15 |
| vLLM greedy output equals one of the reference's greedy outputs | 15/15 |
| reference greedy output stable across its own 4 runs | 8/15 (7 cases flip on near-tie tokens) |
| trajectory tokens generated | 0/15 |

Where outputs differ between runs, the alternatives say the same thing: for example "roadwork" vs "road work", grounding box corners 1–3 units apart, or reworded reasoning with the same meta-actions. A run with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (5 of these requests) completed with no sync errors.

**LingoQA**

The official evaluation protocol: 500 questions, front camera, 5 frames each, greedy, up to 256 tokens. Each answer is scored with `wayveai/Lingo-Judge` as the maximum over all references, with a `> 0` threshold.

| | Lingo-Judge accuracy |
|---|---|
| reference implementation (transformers, SDPA, bf16) | 81.0% (405/500) |
| this PR | 80.8% (404/500) |

476/500 answers are identical; the other 24 are near-tie wording variants. The model card reports 79.2.

**Performance**

The same weights served as plain Qwen3-VL, i.e. the converted `vlm.` weights on the unmodified build, were compared with this PR on the released checkpoint. The workload was 20 single requests plus 10 × 6 concurrent requests, each with 24 images and about 4.6k prompt tokens.

| median | plain Qwen3-VL | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TTFT | 0.661 s | 0.661 s |
| decode | 20.52 ms/token | 20.52 ms/token |
| request latency | 0.909 s | 0.915 s |
| 6 concurrent requests, wall time | 0.982 s | 0.983 s |

**Tests**

- New: `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_alpamayo2_super.py` (tokenizer ids against `traj_ids`, trajectory tokens in text, the per-image pixel budget, video rejection, and the weight mapper). Only small metadata files are downloaded.
- These pass: `tests/models/test_registry.py`; `test_common.py`, `test_tensor_schema.py` and `test_initialization.py` filtered with `-k Alpamayo2`.
- `tests/transformers_utils`, `tests/renderers` and `tests/config` cover the shared registries touched here. They give the same results with and without this change.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes, including mypy, markdownlint and the CI-wiring check.

## Details

- **Weights.** The checkpoint stores Qwen3-VL under `vlm.` and the trajectory expert under `expert.`. The `WeightsMapper` rewrites `vlm.` onto the Qwen3-VL layout and drops `expert.`.
- **Config.** `model_type: alpamayo2_super` is not in transformers. `Alpamayo2SuperConfig` exposes the nested `vlm_config` as a `Qwen3VLConfig` and keeps the trajectory fields. It matches vLLM-Omni's config class field for field, so vLLM-Omni can use this one once its vLLM pin includes it.
- **Tokenizer.** The checkpoint ships the base Qwen3-VL tokenizer, and the reference appends 4,000 `<iN>` trajectory tokens and 29 special tokens in code. The model's embeddings and `traj_ids` assume those ids. The `alpamayo2_super` tokenizer mode appends them the same way and checks them against `traj_ids`. It is auto-selected for the architecture, uses `HfRenderer`, and needs no `--tokenizer-mode`. Without it, prompts with trajectory tokens would tokenize as plain text.
- **Trajectory-token mask.** Like the reference (`MaskDiscreteTrajectoryLogitsProcessor`), `compute_logits` never samples the discrete trajectory tokens, because they only appear in prompts. Clients cannot do this themselves: `logit_bias` is capped at 1,024 entries. The mask is a single slice assignment on the logits, with no host sync.
- **Pixel budget.** The model config sets `min_pixels=163840` and `max_pixels=196608`, and the reference implementation passes them to the processor for every task (`helper.get_processor`). The limit applies to each image separately, so it is the same whether a request has one camera or six. The checkpoint's preprocessor config doesn't carry it, so it is set on `image_processor.size` as in `d3.py`; `mm_processor_kwargs` can still override it.
- **Image-only.** The reference implementation passes camera frames as images and never uses video, so `get_supported_mm_limits` lists only `image`; a video input is rejected with a 400 (`At most 0 video(s) may be provided in one prompt`). Qwen3-VL's `get_supported_mm_processor_kwargs` assumes video is supported, so the base implementation is used instead.
- **Relation to vLLM-Omni.** vllm-project/vllm-omni#9133 registers its trajectory reasoning stage as `Alpamayo2SuperPolicy`, so with vLLM-Omni installed, `Alpamayo2Super` still resolves to this class. A follow-up there can subclass this class.
- **Limitations.**
  - No trajectories (that needs the expert) and will be covered in vLLM-Omni
  - Pipeline parallelism and LoRA are inherited from Qwen3-VL but were not tested.
  - CI does not run the full checkpoint (72 GB, 62.5 GiB in bf16), so the end-to-end parity above was run locally.

**AI assistance.** The code, tests, validation scripts and this description were written with Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code). I reviewed all changed lines and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Multimodal] Skip encoder towers on later PP stages under V2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Model Runner V2 runs multimodal encoders on the first pipeline stage only, but every stage still builds and loads the encoder towers. This skips them on the later stages through the existing `_mark_tower_model` path.

## Claims

- With PP under V2, later stages no longer allocate or load encoder towers: PP1 model loading drops by the tower size (0.58 GiB on LLaVA-1.5-7B, 0.62 GiB on Qwen3.5-4B, 0.85 GiB on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 1.27 GiB on Ultravox v0.5).
- Outputs are unchanged: image outputs under PP match HF in `llava-broadcast` run with PP=2, and the existing PP comparison tests pass.
- Encoder tower construction and loading are unchanged for PP=1, the first stage and the V1 runner.

## Validation

All runs on main (`6ad2e06c4a`) with and without this commit, two sm_80 GPUs, V2 runner, FlashInfer sampler off.

```text
pytest tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py -k test_tp_multimodal_generation   # 3 passed (main and this change)
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py                                          # 9 passed
```

`llava-broadcast` (image outputs compared against HF) was also run with PP=2 instead of TP=2. It checks short eager image generations under PP; it passes on main too, so it does not guard the memory saving, which the loading numbers below show. `test_tp_multimodal_generation` compares text completions only; it does not send image or audio inputs. Ultravox's Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct backbone is gated for this account, so it was taken from the ModelScope mirror, checked byte-identical to the Hugging Face repository at `9213176726` by file hashes, and run offline.

PP0 / PP1 model loading:

| Model | main | this change | without PP |
|---|---|---|---|
| LLaVA-1.5-7B | 6.86 / 6.86 GiB | 6.86 / 6.28 GiB | |
| InternVL3-1B | 1.17 / 1.17 GiB | 1.17 / 0.59 GiB | 1.76 GiB |
| Ultravox v0.5 (Llama 3.2 1B) | 2.68 / 2.68 GiB | 2.68 / 1.41 GiB | 3.59 GiB |

What remains above the single-stage size on Ultravox is the input embedding and LM head that PP keeps on separate stages.

Serving Qwen3.5-4B (BF16) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 with PP=2 (`--max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8`), five greedy chat requests (two text, two with one image, one with two images) with logprobs; main was served twice per model:

| | Qwen3.5-4B main | this change | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B main | this change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PP1 model loading | 5.27 GiB | 4.65 GiB | 11.28 GiB | 10.43 GiB |
| PP1 memory in use (`nvidia-smi`) | 58,612 / 58,632 MiB | 57,960 MiB | 58,824 / 58,852 MiB | 57,970 MiB |
| PP0 model loading | 5.27 GiB | 5.27 GiB | 11.01 GiB | 11.01 GiB |
| KV cache | 2,746,044 tokens | 2,746,044 tokens | 3,349,038 tokens | 3,349,038 tokens |

Qwen3.5-4B is identical in tokens and logprobs on all five requests across both main runs and this change. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is not deterministic on main itself (the two main runs diverge on two requests, at tokens 47 and 119); against the second main run this change diverges on the other two (tokens 14 and 120) and the remaining three have the same tokens with slightly different logprobs, so these runs do not separate the effect of the change from run-to-run noise on that model. The KV cache is sized by PP0, which still holds the tower, so it does not grow there; the first main run of each model compiled from a cold cache and is left out of the KV row.

The compiled extensions came from a build that adds two unrelated kernels to main's sources; no kernel these models use differs from main.

## Details

`_mark_tower_model` already builds a tower on the meta device and wraps it in `StageMissingLayer` when `--limit-mm-per-prompt` is 0 for all of its modalities, and `AutoWeightsLoader` skips the weights of a `StageMissingLayer`. This adds a second condition to the same skip: the V2 runner and not the first stage. Under V2 the encoder only runs where `supports_mm_inputs and is_first_pp_rank` holds; the encoder cache, the encoder runner and the encoder CUDA graphs only exist on the first stage, and no `get_mrope_input_positions` implementation, which every stage runs, touches a tower. V1 is left out because its `profile_run` calls `embed_multimodal` on every rank.

Models that branch on a missing tower: Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-VL-MoE and Qwen3-Omni turn `use_deepstack` off on later stages, which do not use it since deepstack inputs are consumed on the first stage; the PP `start_layer` check of Qwen3-VL and Qwen3-VL-MoE reads the config, so it still runs, and Qwen3-Omni has none. Qwen4Exp gated that check on `use_deepstack`, so it now reads the config, matching Qwen3-VL and Qwen3-VL-MoE, including when multimodal inputs are disabled. The checked Qwen4Exp checkpoints have an empty `deepstack_visual_indexes`, so the assertion passes for them. Pixtral and Llama 4 only use a missing tower to skip its weights.

About 100 model files build their towers through this helper; the GPU runs above cover the models listed.

No open PR covers this: searches for `_mark_tower_model`, `StageMissingLayer` and pipeline-parallel encoder or tower changes return nothing related.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Match reasoning delimiters by token identity
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make the Rust reasoning parsers built on `DelimitedReasoningParser` (Qwen3, DeepSeek R1 / V3 / V4 / V4.1, GLM-4.5 / 4.7, Kimi K2, MiMo, Kimi, Cohere, Seed-OSS, MiniMax M2 / M3, Step3 / 3.5 / 5, Nemotron V3, Hy) end reasoning only at the dedicated end-delimiter token, so `</think>` written with ordinary tokens (the model quoting the tag) stays reasoning. This matches how the Python parsers detect these delimiters while streaming. Independent of the DSML tool-parser stack (#62874 → #62875); no shared files.

## Claims

- An ordinary-token `</think>` (or the family's end delimiter) inside reasoning no longer ends reasoning and leaks the rest of the reasoning into content.
- An ordinary-token start delimiter in content stays content.
- An ordinary partial delimiter (`</thi`) streams immediately instead of being held back.
- MiniMax M3 drops a response-leading `</mm:think>` only when it is the dedicated token.
- Output with the dedicated tokens parses exactly as before.

## Validation

From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo nextest run --workspace --features vllm-parser/test-util --no-fail-fast   # 2233 passed, 13 skipped
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features vllm-parser/test-util -- -D warnings
```

- **New tests** (`reasoning/tests.rs`, `reasoning/minimax_m3.rs`): every delimited family (table of nine constructors, with each family's own delimiters) ends reasoning at the dedicated end token and keeps an ordinary-token copy of it as reasoning; an ordinary start delimiter stays content; an ordinary partial end delimiter streams immediately; M3 keeps an ordinary leading `</mm:think>` as content. Dedicated delimiters split at every byte across chunks are covered by the existing framing tests.
- **Fails before the fix.** The new tests run against the current implementation (first commit of this PR, which only changes tests):

  ```text
  $ cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser --features test-util reasoning   # new tests on the current implementation
  FAIL reasoning::tests::delimited_families_end_reasoning_only_at_the_dedicated_end_token
       left: "quote "      right: "quote </think> then"
  FAIL reasoning::tests::delimited_ordinary_start_delimiter_stays_content
       left: Some(DecodedText { text: "x", .. })   right: None   # reasoning
  FAIL reasoning::tests::delimited_ordinary_partial_end_delimiter_streams_immediately
       left: Some("reason")   right: Some("reason</thi")
  FAIL reasoning::minimax_m3::tests::minimax_m3_keeps_ordinary_leading_end_marker
       left: None          right: Some("</mm")
  Summary 79 tests run: 75 passed, 4 failed
  ```

  With the fix all 79 pass.
- **Existing behavior:** all existing reasoning, unified (combined, Hy), chat, and server tests pass. They now feed decoded output in the serving shape (see the first commit), so they cover the dedicated-token path for every family: framing newlines, prompt-derived initial state, partial delimiters split across chunks, zero-width tokens, and token-attribution conservation.
- **End to end with real tokenizers:** the chat `roundtrip` `reasoning_and_content` cases (`rust/src/chat/tests/roundtrip.rs`) render with the native renderer, tokenize with the real checkpoint tokenizers, decode through the production decoder, and parse reasoning through the guarded delimiters for Qwen3, Qwen3.5, MiMo, MiniMax M2.5 / M3, DeepSeek V4 / V4.1, GLM-4.5 / 4.7, Seed-OSS, Step3.5, Step-5, and Nemotron V3.
- No GPU serving run or accuracy eval. With the dedicated tokens, parser output is unchanged; only ordinary-token spellings of the delimiters behave differently.

## Details

**Two commits.**

1. *Test-only:* reasoning tests fed `DecodedText::unattributed` text, gave delimiter tokens synthetic IDs, or had mock engines emit `<think>` as byte tokens. They now feed output in the serving shape: `vllm_tokenizer::test_utils::decode_chunks` encodes the chunks with the test tokenizer's configured tokens, decodes them through the incremental decoder, and splits at the chunk boundaries. Parser behavior is unchanged in this commit; the full suite passes on the current implementation.
2. *Fix:* `DelimitedReasoningParser` builds its delimiters, with their optional framing text, as `Marker`s guarded by the token IDs the builder already resolves (a family whose tokenizer lacks a delimiter token already fails construction with `MissingToken`), and matches them through the shared marker scanner over the attributed buffer, the utilities added for Kimi K3 in #58358. MiniMax M3's drop of a response-leading `</mm:think>` uses the same guarded marker.

**Root cause.** The parser found the delimiter with `str::find` and held back partial matches with `partial_prefix_len`, so it could not tell the dedicated token from the same bytes spelled by ordinary tokens.

**Why token identity, and why for every family.** The Python parsers already detect these delimiters by token ID when streaming. The parser engine treats `token_id_terminals` that resolve in the vocabulary as strict once it has seen token IDs (`streaming_parser_engine.py`, `_process_lex_tokens`), and the legacy thinking parsers end reasoning only when `end_token_id in delta_token_ids`. Feeding `A ` + ordinary-token `</think>` + ` B` + dedicated `</think>` + `C` through `ParserManager` on `main` with the real tokenizers gives reasoning `A </think> B` / content `C` when streaming for `deepseek_v4`, `deepseek_v3`, `deepseek_r1`, `qwen3`, `glm45`, `glm47`, `mimo`, `kimi_k2`, `minimax_m2`, `seed_oss`, `step3p5`, and `step5`. Two exceptions:

- Python's non-streaming path splits by text, because `DelegatingParser.parse` calls `extract_reasoning(model_output)` without token IDs. So one output parses differently in Python depending on `stream`. The Rust parser uses one state machine for both and follows the streaming behavior.
- The legacy Python `minimax_m3` reasoning parser matches by text in both paths, while `</mm:think>` is an added token; the M3 engine parser config already lists `<mm:think>` / `</mm:think>` as token-ID terminals.

DeepSeek's own streaming output parser for V4 / V4.1 also matches `</think>` only as the added token ([deepseek-recipe `output_parser.rs`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe/blob/935817c66f5d6e64838f419692545f06787e485f/deepseek-recipe/src/stream/output_parser.rs#L338-L408)).

**Known limitations:**

- The reasoning region of the output grammar still ends at the delimiter text. Under a reasoning-aware constrained decode, an ordinary-token `</think>` would end reasoning for XGrammar but not for the parser. The model strongly prefers the dedicated token, so this is unlikely. A token-level end boundary (supported by XGrammar 0.2.7) is a separate change.
- Callers must feed attributed output; fed unattributed text, the parser never crosses a delimiter. The serving path and the chat roundtrip harness are attributed.

Not a duplicate: open PRs touching reasoning parsers add or fix individual Python or Rust parsers; none changes how the Rust delimited parser matches delimiters.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix maximum image token profiling for Unlimited-OCR
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix Unlimited-OCR's underestimated maximum image-token bound, which can reject valid images with a small encoder budget.

## Claims

- Use a 1×32 profiling crop grid to cover the maximum number of newline features.
- Correct the default per-image bound from 3553 to 3793 tokens.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_unlimited_ocr.py -v
```

- New regression: 1 passed; it fails on the original code. Existing processor regression tests: 9 passed. Pre-commit passed.
- Actual `baidu/Unlimited-OCR` serving, BF16 / TP=1, official nightly `0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82`, using a 640×20480 image:

| `max_num_batched_tokens` | Original | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | HTTP 400: 3793 image tokens exceed the 3553 cache | HTTP 200 |
| 8192 | HTTP 200 | HTTP 200 |

Small, ordinary, tall and wide synthetic inputs were compared. Same-budget default compile/graph comparisons preserve output tokens and sampled-token logprobs exactly.

Serving used `TRITON_ALLOW_NON_CONSTEXPR_GLOBALS=1` for an unrelated nightly compile issue. Baseline OCR on some synthetic inputs is empty or incorrect; validation covers request acceptance and output regression, without an accuracy claim.

## Details

Both 4×8 and 1×32 grids contain 32 crops, but the latter has more feature rows and therefore more newline tokens. It reaches the true upper bound without changing inference computation.

No matching open fix was found. Related [#54527](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54527) concerns processor kwargs rather than this default crop-grid bound.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU] Reject unsupported --kv-cache-dtype at CPU attention backend selection
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #62664. The CPU platform now rejects `--kv-cache-dtype` values its attention backends can't handle, at backend selection instead of silently accepting them.

## Claims

- `turboquant_*`, `ultraquant_4bit`, `nvfp4` and `int8_per_token_head` on CPU fail at startup with a clear `ValueError`. Before this, turboquant/ultraquant ran and produced garbage (see the issue).
- `fp8*` is accepted only on hosts with AVX-512 or AMX, the same rule the kernel already enforces after weight loading.
- The MLA path on CPU accepts only unquantized dtypes.
- `auto`, `bfloat16` and `float16` are unchanged.

## Validation

macOS arm64 (Apple M4 Pro), CPU source build, on main @ e4a676cdc2.

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py -k "kv_cache_dtype_validation or rejects_quantized"` | 6 failed, 5 passed | 11 passed |
| `test_cpu_attn.py`, `tests/platforms/test_cpu.py`, `test_attention_selector.py`, `tests/config/test_kv_cache_dtype.py` | | 912 passed, 0 failed (x86-only cases skipped) |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | | passed |
| `LLM("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", kv_cache_dtype=...)` | `auto` OK; `turboquant_k8v4` garbage; `fp8` fails after weight load | `auto` OK ("Paris"); `turboquant_k8v4`, `ultraquant_4bit`, `fp8` raise `ValueError` before weight load |

I could not run on x86. The AVX-512 path, where fp8 is accepted, is covered by the test through a monkeypatched ISA check.

Update: @adenzhou1350 independently tested this on Linux x86 with AVX-512 (no AMX): the 11 tests pass, the parent commit fails 6, and `turboquant_k8v4` is rejected before weight loading (see their comment).

## Details

- Root cause: unlike CUDA/ROCm/XPU, `CpuPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls` never checked the backend's supported KV cache dtypes, so `CPUAttentionBackend.supported_kv_cache_dtypes` was never enforced. The CPU kernel treats any dtype other than fp8 as `auto`, so the unsupported formats got bf16 writes into a uint8 cache.
- I override `supports_kv_cache_dtype` instead of calling the full `validate_configuration`. The full check also validates head size and block size, which would change behaviour for models that work today.
- Custom dtypes registered through #52670 are rejected on CPU until the CPU backend declares support for them.
- Compatible with #61168: its `ultraquant_4bit` routing returns before this check, and the test doesn't parametrize `ultraquant_4bit`.
- CI: the test is in `test_cpu_attn.py` (CPU kernel tests job). That job doesn't list `vllm/platforms/cpu.py` as a dependency. I left the CI config alone.

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line and ran the checks above myself.

## Purpose

`Renderer.validate_token_ids` skips the vocab range check when there is no
tokenizer, so with `--skip-tokenizer-init` out-of-range prompt token ids are
not rejected. This runs the check whenever token ids are present, using the
model vocab size as the bound when there is no tokenizer.

No existing PR covers this.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Expect 400 from /v1/embeddings for bge-m3 token_embed
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

`test_bge_m3_api_server_embedding[token_embed]` fails on both AMD and NVIDIA with `openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 ... 'loc': 'body.encoding_format', 'msg': "Input should be 'float'", 'input': 'base64'`. It is the only failure in both `Language Models (Extended Pooling)` steps of nightly 96581.

AMD: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96581/list?sid=01a16238-14cb-410a-ab01-df25ca5154c3
NVIDIA: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96581/list?sid=01a16238-1564-453c-9761-954f5e42564f

## Cause

#61772 made the `token_embed` task serve `/v1/embeddings` itself through `TokenEmbeddingRequest`, which accepts only `encoding_format="float"`. That restriction is intentional, and the same PR asserts in `test_factories.py` that `base64` on this route returns 400.

The OpenAI client sends `encoding_format="base64"` by default, so for `token_embed` the request is now rejected at validation with 400 instead of reaching the old 500. The bge-m3 test still expected `InternalServerError` for every non-`embed` task.

## Fix

Expect `BadRequestError` for `token_embed` and keep `InternalServerError` for `token_classify`, which still behaves as before. The server is not changed.

## Test plan

`pytest -v -s models/language/pooling/test_bge_m3.py::test_bge_m3_api_server_embedding` passes for `embed`, `token_embed` and `token_classify` on MI300X.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Include multimodal limits in the model compile-cache hash
commits.pr_body:
## Problem Description:

If we start VLLM_CACHE_ROOT first with vision enabled, next time, if vision is disabled, because the currently way of hashing kernel cache miss the multimodal config, the start will run into compilation error. 


## Reproduction

On `main` (nightly `0.32.1rc1.dev80+gaa3564cee`, torch 2.14.0+cu130), Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct,
one H100. The cache must be primed by a multimodal start first — a cold start in text-only mode
compiles fresh and succeeds, which is why this is easy to miss.

Verified in Qwen, Gemma (E4B) model for this issue. 

```bash
MODEL=Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct

# step 1: normal multimodal start, then stop the server
VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/cache vllm serve $MODEL --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --port 9256

# step 2: restart text-only, same VLLM_CACHE_ROOT, everything else identical
VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/cache vllm serve $MODEL --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --port 9256 \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}'
```

Step 1 serves. Step 2 dies 28s in, with following error code:

```
(APIServer pid=3301) INFO 10-19 12:08:33 [model.py:951] All limits of multimodal modalities supported by the model are set to 0, running in text-only mode.
(EngineCore pid=3534) INFO 10-19 12:08:49 [decorators.py:326] [backbone] Directly load AOT compilation from path /tmp/cache-main/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/3eb6adbfc35c973cac9a39329f88b47625d56b5c4a1f1b34636cb2059c5a84cd/rank_0_0/model
...
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]   File "/tmp/env-main/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_vl.py", line 2107, in forward
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]     hidden_states = self.language_model.model(
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]   File "/tmp/env-main/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/compilation/decorators.py", line 604, in __call__
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]     output = self.aot_compiled_fn(self, *args, **kwargs)
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]   File "/tmp/env-main/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/_dynamo/aot_compile.py", line 244, in __call__
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]     return self.fn(*args, **kwargs)
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]   File "/tmp/env-main/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2.py", line 402, in forward
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]     def forward(
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]   File "/tmp/env-main/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/_compile.py", line 54, in inner
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]     return disable_fn(*args, **kwargs)
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]   File "/tmp/env-main/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/_dynamo/eval_frame.py", line 1548, in _fn
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]     return fn(*args, **kwargs)
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]   File "/tmp/env-main/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/_dynamo/utils.py", line 5737, in call_size
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]     return x.size(i)
(EngineCore pid=3534) ERROR 10-19 12:08:49 [core.py:1552]            ^^^^^^

...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}
```

With this patch, the same two commands both serve — step 2 compiles its own artifact instead of
loading step 1's:

```
(APIServer pid=5961) INFO 10-19 12:11:35 [model.py:960] All limits of multimodal modalities supported by the model are set to 0, running in text-only mode.
(EngineCore pid=6195) INFO 10-19 12:12:04 [decorators.py:752] [backbone] saved AOT compiled function to /tmp/cache-pr/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/f024ffb13e89a1a3ddb5037cdeda7b8ffef15694850fae6f40313aabd7281ce7/rank_0_0/model
(EngineCore pid=6195) INFO 10-19 12:12:04 [monitor.py:62] [backbone] torch.compile took 13.75 s in total
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

The compile-cache directories are the collision, stated directly. 
You can see that the first line below, without the fix, the torch compile cache will resolve to the same hash ID, leading to the error. After the fix, two compiled cache exist which saves it from crashing. 

```
# main
$ ls /tmp/cache-main/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile
3eb6adbfc35c973cac9a39329f88b47625d56b5c4a1f1b34636cb2059c5a84cd

# with this patch
$ ls /tmp/cache-pr/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile
c58806f08c4d51e4f80badbf7f5ee0ee41a15f2433f57056b64bebda80112368
f024ffb13e89a1a3ddb5037cdeda7b8ffef15694850fae6f40313aabd7281ce7
```

Extend the existing `if self.multimodal_config:` block with the two remaining switches that decide
whether the MM code path runs.

## Test Plan

- Unit test: Adding: New regression tests in `tests/config/test_multimodal_config.py`:
  `test_zero_mm_limits_affect_model_hash`, `test_enable_mm_embeds_affects_model_hash`. Both fail on
  base (the two `compute_hash()` results are identical) and pass with the change.
- E2E Test: End-to-end `vllm serve` reproduction above, plus `lm_eval` and `vllm bench serve` on both arms —
  raw logs in the review thread. Greedy decoding at one request at a time is byte-identical
  between `main` and this patch in both multimodal and text-only mode, as expected for a change
  that only adds entries to a hash computed once at startup.


### 3. Benchmark

#### LM Eval:

The config should not introduce any code regression in quality as it relates to compile kernel cache only. Tested in four cases: Mutlimodal on without PR, mutlimodal on with PR; Text only without PR; Text only with PR. 

32 fixed prompts, `temperature 0`, **one request at a time** so continuous batching cannot
introduce reduction-order noise:

```

$ diff greedy_main_text.txt greedy_pr_text.txt  && echo "text: identical"
mm:   identical
text: identical

All four byte-identical -- `main` and this PR, multimodal and text-only, same 32 completions. The
two text-only cells also match the two multimodal ones, which is the expected result for text
input: the two graphs differ in how tokens are handed in (`inputs_embeds` vs `input_ids`), not in
the arithmetic.

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args "base_url=http://127.0.0.1:9256/v1/completions,model=$MODEL,num_concurrent=1,tokenized_requests=False" \
  --tasks gsm8k --limit 100 --trust_remote_code
```
