commits.pr_title: [Security] Refresh Python and runtime CA certificates
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Refresh Python and Ubuntu runtime CA bundles following the [eMudhra certificate incident](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com). This certificate-only change is split out of #62835 so it can be reviewed and merged independently of the other dependency upgrades.

## Claims

- Require `certifi>=2026.10.19` in runtime and documentation inputs, and regenerate all five compiled requirements files. Python's [incident guidance](https://discuss.python.org/t/information-for-python-users-regarding-emudhra-emsign-ca-certificate-security-incident/109576) recommends this minimum.
- Explicitly install `ca-certificates` after `apt-get update` in `vllm-runtime-base`, refreshing the OS trust store used by default `aiohttp` and Rust/native TLS clients. Descendant runtime and test images inherit the bundle when rebuilt.
- Keep the patch limited to certificate inputs, generated certificate pins, the runtime package list, and associated documentation/lint configuration. LMCache and other library upgrades remain in #62835.

## Validation

- Regenerated all five locks using uv 0.11.1 and the exact platform, backend, constraint and exclusion arguments in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`. All applicable `pre_commit run --files <changed files>` hooks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Inspected all layers of Linux AMD64 `nvidia/cuda:13.0.3-base-ubuntu24.04`, platform manifest `sha256:97d085a7423ee18ec483a2878b9be2c976dc4ba908aef96518beb00e1899dcc4`. Its `ca-certificates=20240203` bundle trusts both `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` and `AAA Certificate Services`.
- Extracted the certificates from Ubuntu's [fixed package](https://security.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/pool/main/c/ca-certificates/ca-certificates_20260816ubuntu0.24.04.1_all.deb). Loaded both bundles independently with Python `ssl.SSLContext.load_verify_locations` and checked `get_ca_certs()`: both affected roots are present before the update and absent from the fixed package. The `certifi==2026.10.19` bundle also excludes both roots.
- Confirmed that the Dockerfile change only adds the runtime package and leaves stage dependencies unchanged. Docker is unavailable on this macOS host: the graph hook skips regeneration, and a full container rebuild/in-container TLS test remains pending. No model or inference code changes; model evaluations were not run.

## Details

Updating certifi does not update the operating-system trust store. Installing other runtime packages does not guarantee that an already-installed `ca-certificates` package gets upgraded. Listing it explicitly in the existing runtime installation step selects the current package from freshly updated APT metadata; rebuilding images against a mirror carrying the patched distro package is required. The shared-stage documentation explains this complementary coverage.

**Duplicate-work check:** searched open PRs for the incident, certifi and ca-certificates, and inspected the related diffs. #62835 now contains only the other dependency fixes; its certificate changes are removed by this split. #51503 adds certificates to a separate standalone Rust Dockerfile, not this shared CUDA runtime stage. #59667 covers ongoing dependency-refresh automation and remains separate. Both this PR and #62835 target `main` independently.

AI assistance was used to prepare and validate this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep completion derender stream logprob offsets aligned with tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Keep streaming completion derender logprob offsets aligned with reported token strings, matching batch derender and the coupled completion fix in #60668.

## Claims

- A special token filtered from response text no longer shifts subsequent streaming `logprobs.text_offset` backwards relative to batch output.
- Missing/empty logprob metadata retains the existing emitted-text fallback; response text and token IDs are unchanged.

## Validation

Before the fix, the final regression/neighbor selection returned **2 failed, 14 passed**; with the fix, **16 passed**. The two failures are the skip-special-token cases at chunk sizes 1 and 2. With `ignore_eos=true`, `hello`, `</s>`, ` world` produced streaming offsets `[0,5,5]` versus batch `[0,5,9]`; the fix gives `[0,5,9]` in both modes.

Before publication, copied the complete tracked source at `b05ede56168b5718c425c1493914e5e79f6b8181` (including merged #62114) into an isolated Linux CPU validation directory, applied this patch, and ran both the offset selections and #62114's generated-ID regression together: **22 passed, 147 deselected in 5.94s**, exit 0.

```sh
docker exec -w /validation/completion-offset-submit-20261017 \
  -e PYTHONPATH=/validation/completion-offset-submit-20261017:/validation \
  -e VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
  vllm-tokenizer-validation-20261013 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -p completion_offset_local_assets -p completion_ids_local_assets \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
  -k 'TestStreamLogprobs or TestDerenderCompletionStream or preserves_requested_token_ids' \
  -q --disable-warnings
```

Local plugins use a real cached OPT tokenizer instead of the unavailable default tiny-Llama fixture and skip the full distributed/environment/memory cleanup. They do not replace production derender methods. Those original runs did not exercise the default fixture. Standard regression selection:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  -k 'TestStreamLogprobs or TestDerenderCompletionStream' -v
```

A separate normal render-module CLI/Uvicorn HTTP A/B probe exercised supplied tokens through `/v1/completions/derender`: 12 cases per variant, covering skip-special false/true, chunk sizes 1/2, and present/missing/empty metadata. Each variant returned 66 POST 200 responses, including empty terminal and usage-only controls. Baseline had six offset/state assertion failures; fixed had none. Other inspected response fields were unchanged. Independent reviews audited the patch and saved HTTP results; they did not rerun HTTP.

Fresh pinned patch-scoped hooks, including mypy and CI test tethering, all passed:

```sh
pre-commit run --files vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
```

Environment: Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.19.0. HTTP evidence is supplied-token postprocessing, not model generation, SSE, model evaluation or GPU inference. Native CPU inference is unavailable because the installed `vllm._C` raises SIGILL; no generation-quality/performance claim is made.

### CI assertion follow-up (`dae25f1497`)

Reproduced `test_completion_stream_logprobs_text_offset_absolute` with the original `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` tokenizer: the next offset is 6, while emitted `hello` has length 5 because the reported logprob token retains a leading space. Updated only the old assertion to use reported-token lengths; production logic and the direct batch/stream parity regression are unchanged.

With that tokenizer (snapshot `9408c553e5c189a7dcdc5a5dbd2feb476b061759`), the focused classes pass **16 tests**, and the broader unit-only selection passes **97 tests**. A negative control restoring emitted-text accumulation fails the updated assertion (`5 == 6`); restoring the fix passes. Patch-scoped pre-commit, including mypy, passes. These runs use CPU postprocessing and a local plugin that only skips GPU/distributed cleanup; there is no tokenizer substitution. GPU/full server integration CI remains unverified locally; an attempted wider selection had seven parser-server setup errors due to an unavailable offline model cache.

## Details

Within a chunk, logprob conversion advances offsets using the reported token strings. Across chunks, derender instead advanced the carried offset by `len(new_text)`. These differ when decoding filters special tokens, so the next chunk restarted too early. Carry the end of the last reported logprob token when available, preserving the prior fallback otherwise.

The existing ordinary-text offset test checks the next chunk offset against the lengths of reported logprob token strings, which may retain a leading space absent from response text. The parametrized regression directly compares stream and batch offsets for filtered/preserved special tokens and both chunk sizes.

Fresh open/all-state searches for `60668 in:body`, `derender offset`, `derender text_offset` and `logprob_text_offset` found no competing fix. Related #59510 handles stops and retains the old offset update; #60918 affects coupled packed logprobs, and #60542 changes generate logprob representation rather than this derender state update. #62114 is already merged and preserves token IDs; this PR is based on that merge and fixes a separate metadata field.

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, testing and review. The submitter also confirmed personally running related tests before requesting publication; the numeric results above are from agent-executed commands.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Load Granite Speech checkpoints saved by Transformers v5
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`ibm-granite/granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus` no longer loads in vLLM. Its checkpoint was re-saved with Transformers 5.19 on 2026-10-21 ([HF revision `e69efe37`](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus/commit/e69efe37f97b6283c61f5a8dadda2b3eb67765d6)), and the text model weights are now named `language_model.model.model.*` instead of `language_model.model.*`. This PR maps the extra level away in `GraniteSpeechForConditionalGeneration`, so both checkpoint layouts load.

It also fixes `test_granite_speech.py::test_models[...granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus...]`, which has failed in `Multimodal Models (Extended Generation 1)` on both NVIDIA and AMD since the checkpoint update (full build [96476](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96476)):

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'model' in GraniteModel.
```

## Claims

- The new `granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus` checkpoint loads, and its outputs match Transformers.
- The previous revision of the checkpoint, and the other Granite Speech checkpoints, load as before. The mapping only touches names starting with `language_model.model.model.`, which no older checkpoint has.

## Validation

GB300, transformers 5.20.2 and peft 0.21.1, matching the CI pins.

| Check | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_granite_speech.py` (3.3-2b with LoRA, 4.0-1b, 4.1-2b-plus) | 4.1-2b-plus fails with the error above | 3 passed |
| Greedy `"The capital of France is"`, 8 tokens, old revision `1454e6e1` | ` Paris.` | ` Paris.` (Transformers: ` Paris.`) |
| Same, new revision `e69efe37` | load error | ` also a city of 20 million people` (Transformers: identical) |

The new revision also switches the text config to YaRN RoPE (factor 4). The test compares against Transformers, so it covers that path too.

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_granite_speech.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/granite_speech.py
```

No separate model evaluation. The change only renames weights at load time, and the test above checks the outputs against Transformers.

## Details

**Why the extra `model.`** Transformers' `granite_speech` conversion mapping has two renamings: a top-level `^language_model.model` → `model.language_model`, and `^language_model.model` → `language_model`, scoped to `GraniteSpeechModel`. The new names are most likely `save_pretrained` reversing both of them. I have not confirmed this in the Transformers source. Transformers applies both renamings on load, so it reads the checkpoint correctly. vLLM loads checkpoint names directly, so it needs the mapping.

**Relation to #60666.** That draft PR applies Transformers' checkpoint renamings in vLLM's loader generically, and would probably make this mapping unnecessary. It is large (122 files) and not ready for review yet. This PR is a minimal fix for users and CI in the meantime. The mapping can be dropped once #60666 lands.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs and issues for `granite speech`, `granite_speech` and `granite-speech-4.1-2b-plus`. Only #60666 touches this model's weight names. Its explicit Granite Speech mapping covers `model.language_model.*`. I have not tested whether its generic renamings handle the double-nested names.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix default multimodal LoRA selection in `/v1/chat/completions/batch`. Select the adapter independently for each conversation instead of passing the entire batch to the single-conversation selector.

## Claims

- Apply default multimodal LoRAs to the appropriate conversations in a batch.
- Preserve explicit adapter precedence and text-only behavior.

## Validation

```bash
uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py \
  -m skip_global_cleanup -q
# 6 passed, 5 deselected

uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/lora/test_serving_models.py -q
# 11 passed

uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \

  vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/batch_serving.py \
  tests/entrypoints/multimodal/openai/chat_completion/test_default_mm_loras.py
# All applicable checks passed
```

Real HTTP validation on an H800 used `ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-2b` and its bundled LoRA, with BF16, eager mode, and `max_num_seqs=1`.

- Before the fix, batch audio requests produced different output from single requests using the default adapter.
- After the fix, audio-only and mixed text/audio batches matched the single-request audio output token for token.
- Text-only, single-request, and explicit-adapter results remained unchanged.

HTTP validation preceded the rebase; the affected files are unchanged. The checks above were rerun after rebasing.

The existing Phi-4 integration test covers single and batch endpoints with default and explicit adapters. These cases are included in CI but were not run locally.

## Details

The adapter selector expects one conversation, but the batch endpoint passed a nested list of conversations. No modalities were detected, so default adapters were silently omitted.

Resolve the adapter from each existing `single_request` before submitting it to the engine.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Bound late chunk sizes in the Python API
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Bound `LateChunkingParams.chunk_size` to `0 < chunk_size < 2**63`, matching the HTTP schema added in #61772.

## Claims

Reject oversized chunk sizes before engine handoff. The maximum valid value, `2**63 - 1`, still works.

## Validation

123 tests passed:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/test_pooling_params.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_pooler_methods.py
```

Pre-commit checks passed. On RunPod with an NVIDIA L4 and `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small`, both model runners passed 7 tests, including the new `LLM.encode` regression, ordinary inputs and mixed chunk sizes:

```bash
for runner in 1 0; do
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=$runner .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
    tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_offline.py \
    -k 'test_late_chunking_rejects_oversized_chunk_size or test_e5_late_chunking_mixed_requests or test_str_prompts or test_token_ids_prompts'
done
```

The new regression changes `chunk_size` to `2**64` after construction, then checks that `LLM.encode` rejects it without leaving unfinished requests.

## Details

Positive integers of `2**64` or more currently pass Python parameter validation but fail MessagePack encoding after the request is registered. The shared guard rejects them during construction and request validation.

Found during [review of #61419](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61419#discussion_r4266235103). #61772 fixed the HTTP schema; this covers the remaining Python API path.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Share orjson responses across render and pooling
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Use shared `create_json_response()` in `api_utils.py` for render, embedding, token-embedding and generic pooling responses. Encode with orjson, including native NumPy input, and simplify hf3fs now that orjson is a required dependency.

Fix #44997. Latest head: `7f06159438` (token-embedding changes in `913437ee00`), including the [integration request](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58660#issuecomment-6333029142) for token embeddings introduced by #61772.

## Claims

- Accept Pydantic models, sequences of models and ready dictionaries. Preserve error statuses, explicit success statuses, integer keys and JSONResponse fallback for unsupported values such as opaque integers outside 64 bits.
- Reuse the helper across the affected render/pooling routes. Keep schemas, vector shapes, late-chunking field omission, usage accounting and binary streaming behavior unchanged. Plain Response objects retain load accounting until response completion.
- Avoid Python-list expansion for native NumPy embedding matrices. Earlier local measurements also show substantially faster serialization of large multimodal render responses; these are microbenchmarks, with no final-orjson end-to-end latency claim.

## Validation

All results below were agent-run. Latest local environment: Apple M3/macOS ARM64, Python 3.12.13, Pydantic 2.13.5, orjson 3.13.0 and PyTorch 2.14.0.

- **85 focused unit tests passed** after syncing main, across token-embedding late-chunking, API-utils, pooling-utils and scoring IO-processor suites. Coverage retains float32, bfloat16, non-contiguous matrices, optional late-chunking metadata and per-document ranges. Updated response tests use real serving/config/renderer constructors and replace only the external engine client. Obsolete response-class parameterization and render spies are removed.
- **Red/green reproduced:** the updated tests against the pre-fix serving file at `53728814b7` fail with the same missing-selector ImportError as CI; restoring the fix and syncing current main yields 85 passes. Relevant output and commands are below.
- The final [remote pre-commit run](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/39731490947) passed at `7f06159438`. All applicable pre-commit hooks on the two changed files passed. Whole-repository **mypy passed**, including a fresh run after syncing main through `5fa7b7b01b`. Full-repository pre-commit was also run: its only failure is an unchanged Docker nonroot-entrypoint shell test on macOS, where case 8 compares logical `/var/...` with physical `/private/var/...` cwd paths. Those scripts match the base revision. No hook or workflow was bypassed or changed for this integration.
- **18 existing real-model online cases collect successfully**, but were not executed locally: the checkout has no built vLLM native extensions/GPU and the A800 SSH connection is closed. Collection is not inference validation. The existing Buildkite Pooling step selects `entrypoints/pooling`, including the `RemoteOpenAIServer` token-embedding and late-chunking tests.
- Earlier full helper/render/pooling validation at `a94771eeda`: 135 unit cases and 18 in-process ASGI checks using stub engine/serving outputs passed. The hf3fs cleanup at `875d2360e7` separately passed 14 existing unit cases and 13 before/after ASGI cases with exact status/body/content-type/length parity. These are earlier-revision results, not fresh model-backed checks for this integration.

The final orjson implementation has **not** been rerun with a real model/GPU or measured end-to-end HTTP latency.

<details>
<summary>Latest integration reproduction</summary>

Before: run the updated tests with the production serving file from `53728814b7`:

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -q \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py \
  -k 'token_embedding_response or online_chunk_ranges'
```

```text
ImportError: cannot import name 'get_json_response_cls' from 'vllm.entrypoints.pooling.utils'
ERROR .../test_late_chunking.py
```

After restoring the fixed serving file:

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -q \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_utils.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py
# 85 passed

pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual
```

On macOS, the external runner applies the existing `skip_global_cleanup` escape to these CPU-only cases to avoid an unrelated PyTorch teardown crash; all test bodies run. No test skip, retry, tolerance change or CI workflow change was added.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Serialization benchmark evidence and limits</summary>

These were earlier agent-run Apple M3 serialization measurements, with deterministic synthetic data. They are not captured production responses.

At `4f0d282288`, compare `create_json_response({"embedding": values})` against the same helper with `values.tolist()`. Values are `np.random.default_rng(42).standard_normal((batch, 1024), dtype=np.float32)`. Three sequential processes, five warmups and 25 randomized-order timing groups, with `max(3, 1024 // batch)` calls per group. Results are medians of the process medians and include conversion, encoding and response construction/destruction.

| Shape | .tolist() + helper | Native NumPy + helper |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1×1024 | 0.0292 ms | 0.0148 ms |
| 8×1024 | 0.2396 ms | 0.1427 ms |
| 32×1024 | 1.0099 ms | 0.6457 ms |
| 128×1024 | 4.5317 ms | 2.7713 ms |
| 512×1024 | 19.8537 ms | 11.1970 ms |

For 512×1024, process medians ranged 19.822–20.392 ms with .tolist() and 11.152–11.323 ms with native NumPy. Parsed values agree within float32 precision. Native float32 emits shorter decimals, matching embedding's prior ORJSONResponse path. Embeddings already used this NumPy path when orjson was installed; this is not an additional speedup over that path.

Render measurements at `e87f2a3a55` use actual GenerateRequest types and deterministic synthetic float32 tensors encoded by vLLM multimodal serde. Timings include `model_dump()`, encoding and response construction/destruction, excluding fixture preparation, model validation and HTTP. Three sequential processes, five warmups and 35 randomized-order timing groups; medians of process medians:

| Synthetic response | Original JSONResponse | Previous Pydantic candidate | Shared orjson helper |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 14.4 MB singleton | 26.591 ms | 7.230 ms | 1.407 ms |
| 57.7 MB singleton | 121.223 ms | 30.622 ms | 5.753 ms |
| 28.9 MB list of two | 55.779 ms | 10.837 ms | 2.690 ms |

For 57.7 MB, process medians ranged 29.879–31.348 ms for Pydantic and 5.650–5.872 ms for the helper. Small text singleton timings were close (3.684 vs. 3.982 µs); Pydantic was faster for a small text list (4.968 vs. 7.222 µs) and cache-hit response (28.396 vs. 31.691 µs). The optimization targets large multimodal responses, with a small absolute cost on those controls.

</details>

## Details

The helper materializes model dictionaries, encodes with `OPT_NON_STR_KEYS | OPT_SERIALIZE_NUMPY`, and returns application/json bytes directly. ErrorResponse retains its JSONResponse/status path. An orjson TypeError falls back to JSONResponse using the materialized content and requested status, preserving arbitrary-size opaque integers without an extra hot-path scan.

The integration with #61772 removes ServingTokenEmbedding's reference to the deleted response-class selector, which otherwise breaks frontend imports and mypy. It now passes its existing dictionary payload to the shared helper and calls the existing ndarray-capable encoder directly, retaining that encoder's dtype fallback. Token/chunk algorithms and response metadata remain those introduced by #61772.

The latest main sync also resolved the import conflict in pooling utilities: preserve main's `dataclasses.replace`/`reserve_tokens` additions while keeping the obsolete response selector removed.

The hf3fs server/client use the required orjson dependency; five server response sites construct ORJSONResponse directly. `orjson>=3.11.6` matches the existing test dependency floor.

Motivated by [llm-d-router #2685](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/2685). This updates the existing render serialization PR: #46722 addresses multimodal preprocessing/transfer size, while #58314 targets ordinary completion responses in a different router.

AI assistance disclosure: Codex prepared the implementation, tests, benchmark analysis and PR updates. Results are agent-run and are not represented as human-run validation.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Move V1 Attention, core kernels and quantization AMD mirrors from fixed to automatic shards
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Moves four AMD mirrors from fixed pytest shards to `automatic_shard`, the way #61200 and #61477 moved their CUDA steps. For each mirror: `parallelism` is dropped, `--shard-id`/`--num-shards` come off the commands, `Shard %N` comes out of the label (the generator adds `shard N/M`), and `automatic_shard: true` is set. No tests change.

| Mirror | Was | Planned shards |
|---|---:|---:|
| `amd-v1-attention-h100-mi300` | 2 fixed | 3 |
| `amd-v1-attention-b200` | 2 fixed | 4 |
| `amd-kernels-core-operation-test` | 3 fixed | 3 |
| `amd-quantization` | 4 fixed | 3 |

The MI300 V1 Attention mirror had two `commands:` keys in one block. YAML keeps only the second, so the first (`pytest -v -s v1/attention`) never ran; it's removed, and the commands that run are the same as before minus the shard arguments.

The Quantization mirror also ran its two `rocm/` test files only on the first shard, behind `if [ "$$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB" = "0" ]`. Those guards come off, so they are plain pytest commands the plan places like any other.

The Extended Pooling mirror was in this PR, but main moved it to a different AMD queue (#61955), which has no per-file timings for it yet. The planner would fall back to one job, close to the step's timeout, so it stays on fixed shards until that queue has timings.

`.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` still carries the old `Shard %N` labels; it's a separate pipeline file and is left as is.

## Test Plan

- Planned each mirror with ci-infra main's `runtime_shard.plan_step` against this branch and main's `amd-<key>` timings on the mirror's own queue.
- Rendered each mirror with the pipeline generator and ran every shard's `VLLM_TEST_COMMANDS` against a mock test tree, as a PR build and with main's `pytest -p ci_otel` wrapper: every test of every command ran in exactly one shard, with the same env.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Support online quantization of Kimi K3 NVIDIA projections
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix online quantization of the Kimi K3 NVIDIA projections, e.g.

```
--quantization-config '{"targets":{"*.in_proj_qkvgfab":"mxfp8","*.fused_qkv_a_g_proj":"mxfp8","*.routed_expert_down_proj":"mxfp8","*.routed_expert_up_proj":"mxfp8"}}'
```

Three places in the model broke:

- **KDA input projection padding.** `in_proj_qkvgfab` pads each TP-local row block for alignment. No checkpoint shard covers that padding, but online processing counted it toward the layer's expected load size, so the layer never reached completion and every KDA layer was deferred to `finalize_layerwise_processing`, keeping all its buffered checkpoint tensors alive until the end of loading. The projection now declares `weight_loader_numel` without the padding. Online processing also rebuilds the weight from uninitialized storage, so the padding is re-zeroed after each shard load (both `weight_loader` and `weight_loader_v2`).
- **Routed output transform.** `KimiRoutedOutputTransform` fused the residual add as `residual.addmm_(x, up_proj.weight.t())`, bypassing the quantized linear method and its scales. The fused add is now used only for an unquantized up-projection; otherwise the layer is called and the residual added in place.
- **Latent MoE tail kernels.** They multiply by the raw `up_proj.weight`, so `LatentMoERunner` now enables the fused tail path (and deferred MoE finalize) only for an unquantized up-projection.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k nvidia_kda_online_loading
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_latent_moe_tail.py -k deferred_finalize
```

The new KDA test (adapted from the reproducer in #61950) loads the merged projection through online processing for 96 heads (padded) and 128 heads (no padding), TP ranks 0 and 3, and both weight loaders (in forward and reverse shard order). It checks that the layer finishes loading, every source tensor is released, the loaded rows match the checkpoint, and the padding is zero (uninitialized storage is filled with NaN to catch it).

End to end: Kimi K3 MXFP4 on GB300, 2P1D (TP8 prefill x 2, DEP16 decode, 32 GPUs), DSpark K4, AgentX agentic traces at concurrency 240 for 3600 s, with and without online MXFP8 quantization of the KDA/MLA input projections, routed expert projections, and (decode only) `o_proj` and the shared experts.

## Test Result

Performance (p90; the perf runs use synthetic acceptance with AL 3.36):

| | Base | Online quant | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | 19,991 | 24,769 | +23.9 % |
| Interactivity (tok/s/user) | 40.0 | 40.5 | +1.2 % |
| E2E latency (s) | 78.2 | 59.8 | -23.4 % |
| TTFT (s) | 21.8 | 12.2 | -43.9 % |
| E2E-normalized interactivity | 6.9 | 12.5 | +79.8 % |

Accuracy (gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, real rejection sampling, 1P1D TP8 + DEP16):

| | Base | Online quant |
|---|---|---|
| strict-match | 0.9606 | 0.9674 |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Normalize beam search scores by generated length
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Beam search divides each beam's cumulative log-prob (a sum over the *generated* tokens) by `(prompt + generated length) ** length_penalty`. It should divide by the generated length only, as Transformers does. With any non-trivial prompt, the prompt length dominates the denominator, so `length_penalty` stops having an effect and beams that hit EOS early win, often with an empty completion. This affects `LLM.beam_search` and `use_beam_search` on `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and speech-to-text, which all share `create_sort_beams_key_function`.

Fixes #2606, which was auto-closed as stale. The earlier fix in #7007 targeted the old V0 `sequence.py` and was never merged, and the bug carried over into the current frontend implementation.

## Claims

- Beams are ranked by `cum_logprob / num_generated_tokens ** length_penalty`, counting a terminating EOS token, as in Transformers' [`_update_finished_beams`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/09a71e5b32a747dbc7805599457e67c956ef212f/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L3531): `topk_log_probs / ((cur_len + 1 - decoder_prompt_len) ** length_penalty)`. Transformers fixed the same bug in huggingface/transformers#27351.
- Beam search no longer prefers empty completions. On `tests/prompts/example.txt` without trailing newlines, the top beam on `main` is EOS-only for 8 of 8 prompts (HF: 1 of 8). With this PR it is 1 of 8.
- HF parity improves. On the exact prompts `tests/samplers/test_beam_search.py` uses, the top beam matches HF on 8/8 prompts instead of 6/8.
- `length_penalty` changes the result again for long prompts. On `main`, the same beam wins for every value from 0 to 2.
- `BeamSearchParams.length_penalty` now has a docstring describing these semantics.

## Validation

All runs used upstream `1f5514ec4`, precompiled, on an RTX 3050 4 GB (torch 2.14.0+cu130) with transformers 5.20.2.

**Regression test** (CPU, existing fake-engine harness): `pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py -k test_beam_search_score_ignores_prompt_length -v`
- `main`: 2 failed. The online path returns `[]` and the offline path returns `[eos]`, i.e. the 1-token EOS beam beats `[11, 11]`.
- This PR: 2 passed.

**Existing tests with this PR:**
| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search_online.py` | 65 passed |
| `pytest tests/samplers/test_beam_search.py -k "not multimodal"` (GPU; includes the HF-parity, concurrency and structured-output tests) | 12 passed |
| `pytest tests/test_request_input_bounds.py tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py -k beam` | 20 passed |
| `pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -k test_batch_completions` (opt-125m server, beam search) | 1 passed |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` | passed |

**HF parity** (TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat, fp16, `beam_width=4`, `length_penalty=1.0`). HF uses `generate(num_beams=4, num_return_sequences=4)` as in `HfRunner.generate_beam_search`; vLLM uses `LLM.beam_search` as in `VllmRunner.generate_beam_search`. `HfRunner` drops pad tokens, and TinyLlama's pad token is its EOS, so a trailing EOS is dropped from vLLM beams before comparing.

| Prompts | max_tokens | Top beam == HF (main → PR) | Beams == HF (main → PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `example.txt` as read by the test (trailing `\n`) | 64 | 6/8 → **8/8** | 24/32 → **30/32** |
| same | 128 | 6/8 → **8/8** | 21/32 → **29/32** |
| `example.txt`, stripped | 64 | 1/8 → **7/8** | 2/32 → **22/32** |
| same | 128 | 1/8 → **5/8** | 2/32 → **11/32** |

The remaining mismatches come from two algorithmic differences this PR does not touch (see Details).

**`length_penalty` sweep.** Prompt: a 590-token chat prompt (the first 2000 characters of `tests/prompts/summary.txt` plus a question with a short answer). Settings: `beam_width=4`, `max_tokens=64`. Each cell is the generated length of the best beam.

| `length_penalty` | 0.0 | 0.5 | 1.0 | 2.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 16 | 16 | 16 | 16 |
| This PR | 16 | 22 | 64 | 64 |

**Online.** `vllm serve TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0`, then `/v1/completions` with `{"prompt": "vLLM is a high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs.", "use_beam_search": true, "n": 4, "max_tokens": 64}`.
- `main`: `choices[0]` is `""` with `finish_reason: "stop"`, `stop_reason: 2`.
- This PR: `choices[0]` is the generated continuation.

`/v1/chat/completions` with beam search returns the same complete answers on both.

## Details

**Root cause.** `get_beam_search_score` divided by `len(tokens)`. `tokens` starts as the prompt (`BeamSearchInstance` and the online path's `tokens=prompt_token_ids`), but `cum_logprob` only sums generated tokens. The helper was adapted from an old Transformers `BeamHypotheses.add` that had the same bug. huggingface/transformers#27351 (v4.36) fixed it there, noting it "would cause an unexpected bias towards generating shorter sequences".

**Why `len(x.logprobs)`.** Every path that extends or completes a beam appends exactly one logprobs entry and adds that token's log-prob to `cum_logprob`. That covers offline steps, online running beams, EOS beams and aborted beams. `tokens` can't be used, because the online path drops the EOS from `tokens` unless `include_stop_str_in_output` is set. The `max(..., 1)` guard still covers a beam aborted before generating anything.

**Behavior change.** Final rankings change only when the compared beams have different generated lengths, which is the intent. Pruning of running beams is unchanged, since every running beam has the same length at each step.

**Not changed.** Two differences from Transformers remain:
- vLLM finalizes every EOS candidate among each beam's top `2 * beam_width` logprobs; Transformers only finalizes those in the global top `num_beams`.
- vLLM has no early-stopping heuristic.

**Related.**
- #59506 adds overflow handling to the same function. It is orthogonal, but it needs a rebase onto the new `(num_generated_tokens, cumulative_logprob, length_penalty)` signature.
- The Rust-frontend beam search in #47705 ports the old formula, including unit tests that encode it. The same `logprobs.len()` change applies there.
- RFC #61880 plans to reuse `get_beam_search_score` for HF-parity scoring.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `beam search length penalty`, `length_penalty`, `get_beam_search_score`, `beam search normalization` and `beam search shorter`. The only related hits are #2606, the stale V0 PR #7007, and #59506 (overflow only). I also checked every open PR touching `vllm/entrypoints/generate/beam_search/` (#59506, #60327, #60550, #52621, #36285, #60787, #49541, #47705): none changes the normalization.

**AI assistance.** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). It helped locate the bug, write the change and test, and run the validation above. I reviewed every changed line and the results.

cc @DarkLight1337

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Return 400 for structurally-corrupted PNG images
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` now catches Pillow's `SyntaxError` ("broken PNG file"), so a request containing a structurally-corrupted PNG fails with HTTP 400 instead of an unhandled HTTP 500.

Fixes #62703. Related: #60303 / #60308 cover the sibling `DecompressionBombError` case in the same except clause; this change covers the `SyntaxError` case, which that PR does not address.

## Claims

- A chat completion containing a corrupt PNG returns **HTTP 400** `BadRequestError: Failed to load image: broken PNG file (chunk ...)` instead of **HTTP 500** `InternalServerError` with the raw Pillow message.
- No behavior change for valid images, or for corrupt inputs already handled by the `OSError` / `UnidentifiedImageError` branches (they keep returning the same 400s).

## Validation

**Unit test** (real-world reproducer bytes — a 79-byte PNG whose stray bytes between the IDAT CRC and IEND shift the chunk stream):

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py -v
# => 20 passed (incl. new test_image_broken_png_rejected)
```

**End-to-end A/B on a real deployment** — `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`df3bd094a`), single H100, `google/gemma-4-26b-A4B-it`; "patched" = same container with this branch's `image.py` overlayed (byte-identical base verified before overlay):

| Request | Nightly (before) | This branch (after) |
|---|---|---|
| Corrupt PNG (reproducer above) | `500 InternalServerError: broken PNG file (chunk b'\x00\x00IE')` | `400 BadRequestError: Failed to load image: broken PNG file (chunk b'\x00\x00IE')` |
| Valid 64×64 PNG | `200` (answers "Red") | `200` (answers "Red") |
| Random non-image bytes | `400 BadRequestError: Failed to load image: cannot identify image file` | `400` (unchanged) |

CI coverage: `tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py` runs in the premerge CPU job (`pytest -m cpu_test multimodal` in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`), which is triggered by both changed paths (`vllm/multimodal/`, `tests/multimodal`).

## Details

**Root cause:** `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` wraps decode failures in a client-facing `ValueError` (`"Failed to load image: ..."`), but its except clause only catches `(OSError, Image.UnidentifiedImageError)`. Pillow raises a plain `SyntaxError` for corrupted chunk structures — it is neither of those — so it escaped unwrapped. The request-level error mapper (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/error_response.py`) promotes `ValueError` to `BadRequestError` (400) but maps unmapped exceptions to `InternalServerError` (500), which is exactly what clients observed.

**Fix:** add `SyntaxError` to the existing except tuple. The wrapping pattern — and therefore the 400 path — already existed and is proven by the A/B table above. A genuine Python `SyntaxError` cannot occur inside this try block (it only calls Pillow and plain attribute reads), so the widened catch cannot mask unrelated failures.

**Not a duplicate:** #60308 (open) adds `DecompressionBombError` to the same clause but does not handle `SyntaxError`; searches of open issues/PRs for "broken PNG" return no results. The two changes compose trivially if both merge.

**Model evaluations:** not applicable — the change only affects how invalid client input is surfaced (HTTP status/message of the error path); it cannot alter model output for accepted requests.

**AI assistance:** this change was prepared with AI assistance (GLM-5.3 via OpenCode) under the direction of, and fully reviewed line-by-line by, the human submitter, who ran all tests and end-to-end validations above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Keep the JinaVL score token when truncating score prompts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`jinaai/jina-reranker-m0` scores the hidden state of a score token (id 100) that `JinaVLForSequenceClassification.post_process_tokens` appends to the prompt. Since #28631, `CrossEncoderIOProcessor` appends it in `get_score_prompt`, before `render` calls `tok_params.apply_post_tokenization`. When `truncate_prompt_tokens` is binding, truncation runs on the prompt that already has the score token. With the default right-side truncation, that cuts the score token off, and `/score` and `/rerank` silently return the classifier output for an ordinary prompt token. This reserves room for the tokens `post_process_tokens` appends: truncation, padding and the length check run with limits reduced by that count, and the tokens are appended afterwards. The reference `compute_score` in the model repo does the same (it truncates to `max_length - 1`, then appends the score token).

## Claims

- With a binding `truncate_prompt_tokens`, jina-reranker-m0 scores match scoring the template truncated to `truncate_prompt_tokens - 1` tokens plus the score token, and the prompt stays within `truncate_prompt_tokens`.
- `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1` on prompts longer than `max_model_len` keeps working: the prompt is truncated to `max_model_len - 1` tokens plus the score token.
- No change for models whose `post_process_tokens` is a no-op (every other cross-encoder). The change stays in `CrossEncoderIOProcessor`, plus a small `reserve_tokens` helper in `vllm/entrypoints/pooling/utils.py`.

## Validation

Real server on `34ac4f96a3` (`jinaai/jina-reranker-m0 --runner pooling --max-model-len 512`, RTX 4090, `--enforce-eager`). `/rerank` with query "What is the capital of France? Please answer briefly and precisely." and two documents (Paris, Berlin). The references are `/pooling` (`task="classify"`) on the explicit template token IDs, truncated, plus the score token.

Short documents (templates of 32 and 34 tokens), `truncate_prompt_tokens=28`:

| | Paris | Berlin |
|---|---|---|
| reference: 27 tokens + score token | 0.9831 | 0.8146 |
| `main` | 0.9857 | 0.9563 |
| this PR | 0.9830 | 0.8142 |

Long documents (templates of 672 and 674 tokens), `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1`:

| | Paris | Berlin |
|---|---|---|
| reference: 511 tokens + score token | 0.9213 | 0.8930 |
| `main` | 0.9380 | 0.9980 |
| this PR | 0.9211 | 0.8914 |

On `main` the irrelevant document scores about as high as the relevant one, or higher. The remaining differences are bf16 noise between batched and single requests.

Tests:

- New `tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py::test_truncation_keeps_jinavl_score_token`, parametrized over `truncate_prompt_tokens=4` and `-1`. Both cases fail on `main` (the score token is cut off) and pass with this PR.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py`: 27 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

## Details

Before #28631, `get_score_prompt` tokenized with truncation, appended the score token, and the serving layer only validated the length. #28631 moved post-tokenization truncation into `render` after `get_score_prompt`, so it now also runs over the appended token.

`render` now shrinks `max_total_tokens`, `truncate_prompt_tokens` and `pad_prompt_tokens` by the number of appended tokens (`reserve_tokens`) (`-1` follows the reduced `max_total_tokens`), tokenizes and truncates with those limits, and then calls `post_process_tokens`. The count is derived once by running `post_process_tokens` on an empty prompt, so the model interface is unchanged. As a side effect, the "maximum context length" in the length error for jina-reranker-m0 reports `max_model_len - 1`, which is the real limit for the template.

An earlier version of this PR appended the token after truncation without reserving room, so the prompt could exceed the limits by one token (thanks to the review for catching that).

Not a duplicate: I found no issue or PR for this (searched "jina-reranker-m0 truncate", "post_process_tokens", "score token truncation rerank", "JinaVL truncate_prompt_tokens"). #55200 validates truncated prompts for the jina-reranker-v3 processor (`JinaRankingIOProcessor`), and #49963 restored `truncate_prompt_tokens` for that processor. Neither touches the JinaVL score token.

AI assistance was used to find this bug, write the fix and the test, and run the validation shown above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Cut stop strings and stop tokens on derender
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Derender was decoding every token generate sent back which meant stop strings and stop tokens came back into the text. This change cuts them the way the engine does. It fixes #57052 and supersedes #59510. 

## Claims

- Batch chat and completions derender cut the stop string and drop the stop token, the same as `vllm serve`. That includes `include_stop_str_in_output`, `min_tokens` and `ignore_eos`.
- `stop_reason` is passed through from generate. If generate doesn't send it (older servers), derender fills it in from what it matched. It stays null for the primary EOS.
- Completions streaming now drops the stop token which chat already did after #61757.
- Streaming derender returns 400 when the request has stop strings and points to `output_mode=text`, as agreed on #47161.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -v
```

- All pass. That includes the live render-server tests and `test_e2e_token_identity`, which checks `encode(derender(ids)) == ids` still holds.
- 19 of the 26 new tests fail without the fix. The other 7 check that nothing extra gets trimmed.
- `test_text_parity_stop_string` now asserts derender == `output_mode=text` == `/v1/completions`, both with a reported `stop_reason` and with the request's stop list. It needs a GPU and I haven't run it yet. It'll need `/ci run`.

## Details

- It reuses `check_stop_strings` from the engine detokenizer. The EOS ids and generation_config included are loaded once in `__init__` instead of on each call.
- The stop token is checked first, then the stop string on the text that's left. A matched string wins as `stop_reason` which is the engine's order.
- The parser still gets the full `token_ids`, like the main server.
- Streaming is a 400 rather than holding text back, so `DerenderStreamState` doesn't change.
- Known gaps:
  - A streaming request sent with no `chat_request` or `completion_request` can't be rejected.
  - With a parser configured, a stop string that overlaps a special token can cut differently from `vllm serve`.
  - Logprobs aren't trimmed.

Thanks to @pOpO1-9 for the original work on #59510.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Require exact strides for moe_forward custom ops
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #52308: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4` outputs garbage under `torch.compile` with the FlashInfer TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE backend. `--enforce-eager` works. The fix changes the tag on `vllm.moe_forward` and `vllm.moe_forward_shared` from `needs_fixed_stride_order` to `needs_exact_strides`.

This supersedes #52383, which I closed: it moved the pad inside the op based on a wrong diagnosis (CUDA-graph replay), and that approach would break the ROCm RMSNorm+pad fusion (#34636). #49092 (`.contiguous()` in `scaled_fp4_quant`) would be a complementary kernel-side safeguard.

## Claims

- GSM8K accuracy for Nemotron-3-Nano NVFP4 on TRTLLM MoE with default compile goes from ~0.01 back to eager parity.
- A new unit test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- The change is two lines and touches no other code path.

## Validation

1x GB300, torch 2.14.0+cu132, default `vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, which selects the FLASHINFER_TRTLLM MoE backend. Evaluated with `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` on all 1319 questions. Every compiled run used fresh `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` and `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` directories (see the cache note in Details).

| Config | Completions, 5-shot, 256 tokens | Chat, thinking off, 1024 tokens, temp 0 |
|---|---|---|
| `--enforce-eager` | 0.303 | 0.882 |
| compile, main | 0.006 (46% invalid) | 0.008 (47% invalid) |
| compile, this PR | 0.299 | 0.890 |

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \
    --max-tokens 1024 --temperature 0 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```

Unit test: `pytest tests/quantization/test_trtllm_nvfp4_hidden_dim_padding.py -v` gives 5 passed. With the old tag, the new test fails with `[(2816, 1)] == [(2688, 1)]`.

The GPU runs used base commit 8a8e2baa02 with this exact patch. Between that commit and this branch's base, the only change under `fused_moe/` is `oracle/fp8.py`.

## Details

**Root cause.** Nemotron-3-Nano has hidden size 2688. The TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE pads it to 2816, and `MoERunner._maybe_pad_hidden_states` applies `F.pad` inside the compiled graph. Inductor fuses the preceding RMSNorm into the padded buffer. Because `needs_fixed_stride_order` only pins stride *order*, Inductor then passes `shared_experts_input` (the unpadded 2688-wide activations) to `moe_forward_shared` as a view into that buffer: `reinterpret_tensor(buf, (s, 2688), (2816, 1), 0)`. The shared expert's NVFP4 linear calls `scaled_fp4_quant`, whose kernel assumes packed rows. Row 0 is read correctly; every later row is read at the wrong offset. Eager mode never creates the alias. With this PR, the generated code passes a separate packed buffer.

**Why this tag.** `needs_fixed_stride_order` was a torch 2.6 workaround. It was already removed from the other MoE custom ops in #19346, #28974 and #33209; these two ops were missed. Since torch 2.8, `needs_exact_strides` has been the default for custom ops (pytorch/pytorch#148063, #150511), so this restores the default behavior.

**Tradeoff.** Inductor may now insert a copy when its preferred layout differs from eager, which in practice means one `(tokens, hidden)` copy per MoE layer when the hidden dim is padded. When no padding happens, inputs are already contiguous and nothing changes. The change adds no host sync. On ROCm, gpt-oss with the AITER RMSNorm+pad fusion uses `moe_forward` with the padded buffer itself, which is contiguous, so it is unaffected.

**Compile cache note.** Changing the op tag does not invalidate the Inductor FX graph cache or the vLLM AOT compile cache. `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` does not bypass the Inductor cache either. A dev install at the same vLLM version may keep loading the old aliased graph until those caches are cleared. Release upgrades are unaffected because the vLLM version is part of the cache key.

**Scope and CI.**
- `needs_fixed_stride_order` still appears in `model_executor/layers/transformers/moe.py`, `models/utils.py` and `qwen3_dflash2.py`. I did not analyze those call sites and left them unchanged.
- The new test runs in the H200 Quantization job. It mocks the MoE layer with `Mock(spec=MoERunnerInterface)` because `get_layer_from_name` asserts that type, and checks only the stride the op receives, so the result is deterministic.
- No existing GSM8K CI config covers TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE with compile: the Nemotron NVFP4 configs in `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor/` use `--enforce-eager` or CUTLASS. I can add one as a follow-up.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR uses `needs_exact_strides` or addresses this stride alias. #52383 (mine, now closed) and #49092 are discussed above. Open PRs #61179 and #61367 touch the same op registration for a different bug.

**AI assistance.** I used Claude Code to investigate, write the patch and test, and run the evaluations. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evals above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Render GPT-OSS chats with Harmony in /tokenize
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

For GPT-OSS, `/tokenize` renders a chat with the model's HF chat template, while the chat route renders it with Harmony. So `/tokenize` returns ids that the chat route never prefills, which breaks the invariant `test_tokenize_matches_render_for_multimodal_input` already states for multimodal input: `/tokenize` matches `/v1/chat/completions/render`. This PR renders GPT-OSS chats in `/tokenize` through `OnlineRenderer.render_chat`, the function the chat route and the render endpoint use.

## Claims

- For GPT-OSS chats, `/tokenize` returns the ids of `/v1/chat/completions/render`. Through the shared `render_chat`, those are the ids `/v1/chat/completions` prefills; that route itself was not run. Before this change they differed for chats with a system message and no tools, and for tool-call histories.
- Other models are unchanged: their chats still go through `preprocess_chat`.

## Validation

Reproducer: `vllm launch render openai/gpt-oss-20b` (GPU-less) serves both `/tokenize` and `/v1/chat/completions/render`. The same messages were posted to both, on main b1ab16c548 and with this PR:

| Messages | main: `/tokenize` / render | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| system, user, assistant | 126 / 125 ids, first difference at 82 | 125 / 125, equal |
| system, user | 105 / 104, first difference at 82 | 104 / 104, equal |
| user | 82 / 82, equal | equal |
| system, user, `tools` | 129 / 129, equal | equal |
| system, user, an assistant tool call and its result, `tools` | 164 / 162 | 162 / 162, equal |
| system, user, `tools: []` | 83 / 83, not equal | equal |

At index 82 `/tokenize` has `"\n\n"` (279) where Harmony has `<|end|>` (200007): the GPT-OSS template ends the developer instructions with `"\n\n"` when no tools follow, and Harmony does not.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py tests/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/test_serving_tokenization.py -q
```

47 passed. The new `test_tokenize_matches_chat_render_for_gpt_oss` starts the GPU-less render server for openai/gpt-oss-20b (config and tokenizer only, about 23 s) and asserts that `/tokenize` and `/v1/chat/completions/render` return the same ids for a chat with a system message. On main it fails on the ids: `At index 71 diff: 364 != 13`.

`pre-commit` ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy and check-test-tethering: passed.

Not run on a GPU: the change affects only the ids `/tokenize` returns. Generation and the chat route are unchanged, so no model eval applies.

```python
T = "the cat sat on a warm mat and then ran to the old red barn"
CHATS = {
    "system,user,assistant": [{"role": r, "content": T} for r in ("system", "user", "assistant")],
    "system,user": [{"role": "system", "content": T}, {"role": "user", "content": T}],
    "user": [{"role": "user", "content": T}],
}

def post(path, body):
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + path, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return json.loads(r.read())

for name, messages in CHATS.items():
    tokens = post("/tokenize", {"messages": messages})["tokens"]
    token_ids = post("/v1/chat/completions/render", {"messages": messages})["token_ids"]
    print(name, len(tokens), len(token_ids), tokens == token_ids)
```
</details>

## Details

Root cause: `ServingTokenization.create_tokenize` calls `OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat` for every chat, which applies the HF chat template. `OnlineRenderer.render_chat` takes its Harmony branch when `model_type` is `gpt_oss`.

The fix: for GPT-OSS, `/tokenize` builds a `ChatCompletionRequest` from the request's chat fields (`TokenizeChatRequest.to_chat_completion_request`) and calls `render_chat`, as `/v1/chat/completions/render` does. Only declared chat fields are copied, so undeclared body fields such as `stream_options` or `reasoning_effort` do not reach the chat request's validation, as in the Rust frontend's `TokenizeChatRequest::into_chat_request`. An empty `tools` list, which `/tokenize` accepts and the chat route rejects, is dropped.

Behaviour changes for GPT-OSS `/tokenize`, which now follows the chat route:
- `add_generation_prompt`, `continue_final_message`, `chat_template` and `chat_template_kwargs` no longer change the ids. The chat route ignores them for GPT-OSS today.
- A `chat_template` sent without `--trust-request-chat-template` is ignored rather than refused, since it is never rendered.

Open question: the Rust frontend's Harmony renderer honours `add_generation_prompt: false` and rejects `continue_final_message`. Doing the same in `_make_request_with_harmony` would apply to the chat route and `/tokenize` together; I left it out of this PR because it changes the chat route.

Why `/tokenize` rather than pointing callers to `/v1/chat/completions/render`: the render endpoint is off unless the server runs with `--enable-scale-out`, while `/tokenize` is always on. The Rust frontend's `/tokenize` already renders GPT-OSS chats with its Harmony renderer, through the same `prepare_text_request` as its chat route.

Related: #33693 (a draft, idle since April) moves Harmony encoding into the renderer layer, which would make this branch unnecessary. #58414 changes how Harmony is detected; this PR reads `online_renderer.use_harmony`, so `/tokenize` keeps following the chat route either way. #52513 fixes a different `/tokenize` vs chat-route mismatch (`reasoning_content`). No open issue or PR covers this one.

commits.pr_title: [Core][Rust Frontend] Report structured-output compile failures as validation errors
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A structured-output constraint that EngineCore fails to compile finishes the request as `FINISHED_ERROR` with no error attached. The Python frontend rarely sees this, because it validates constraints with the backend library before submitting. The Rust frontend cannot, so its clients get HTTP 500 for an invalid regex or grammar, and an empty 200 when llguidance builds a matcher in an error state (for example a schema with `uniqueItems`). This PR reports compile failures with the `validation_error` code that #49625 introduced for backend mismatches, so both frontends return 400, and makes the guidance backend fail compilation instead of continuing with a broken matcher.

## Claims

- When a request's grammar fails to compile, its error output carries `RequestError(code="validation_error", message="Invalid structured outputs: <compile error>")`. Python already maps that code to `VLLMValidationError` (400) since #49625.
- The guidance backend raises on a matcher that reports an error (`Grammar error: ...`) instead of logging a warning and generating nothing.
- The Rust frontend maps `validation_error` to HTTP 400 (an SSE `BadRequestError` event when streaming) and gRPC `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. This also covers #49625's backend-mismatch rejection, which the Rust frontend reported as 500.
- Rust non-streaming `/inference/v1/generate` fails the request on every engine-typed error, as Python raises every `RequestError`; before, only retryable ones did.

## Validation

GPU smoke on GB200, Qwen3-8B with `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser hermes` via `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve`, `main` (`e9cc6244a0`) against this PR. On `main` the Rust frontend sends native HTTP constraints as guidance and parser-built output grammars as xgrammar, and EngineCore keeps the first request's backend, so two request orders cover both backends and #49625's mismatch rejection. Each order ends with a valid request; the engine stays healthy on both builds.

| Order | Request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| guidance first | completions `regex: "("` | 200, empty text | 400 `Grammar error: ... unclosed group` |
| | completions `grammar: "root ::= ("` | 500 | 400 `Failed to convert the grammar from GBNF to Lark ...` |
| | completions json `{"type": "array", "uniqueItems": true}` | 200, empty text | 400 `Grammar error: Unimplemented keys: ["uniqueItems"]` |
| | chat `regex` (composed into an xgrammar tag, mismatch) | 500 | 400 `... only supports one backend per engine ...` |
| xgrammar first | chat `regex: "("` (composed) | 500 | 400 `Regex parsing error at position 2 ...` |
| | chat streaming `grammar: "root ::= ("` | SSE `InternalServerError` | SSE `BadRequestError` |
| | completions `regex` (guidance, mismatch) | 500 | 400 `... only supports one backend per engine ...` |

Tests:

- Python (`tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_guidance.py`, `test_validation.py`, `tests/test_outputs.py`): 104 passed. `test_grammar_compile_error_finishes_only_request` now asserts the error output's `RequestError`; the new `test_backend_guidance_rejects_grammar_matcher_cannot_build` compiles a `uniqueItems` schema. Both fail with the engine changes reverted (`error` is `None`; compilation does not raise).
- Rust: `cargo nextest run --workspace` (2229 passed), clippy, fmt. `engine_request_errors_map_to_http_status` (was `retryable_engine_error_returns_service_unavailable`) runs a retryable and a validation error through completions, chat, and raw generate against the mock engine; `engine_errors_map_to_status_codes` covers gRPC.

## Details

**Root cause.** Grammar compilation runs asynchronously after `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_init`. Since #47312, a failed compilation finishes only that request, through `grammar_compile_error_reqs`, but without a `RequestError`, so every frontend reports an internal error. #49625 added `validation_error` for the separate case where a request names a backend other than the one the engine already uses; that check runs in `grammar_init`, before compilation, and does not cover a constraint that the right backend fails to compile. The guidance backend creates its `LLMatcher` without failing on a build error: `check_error()` only logs it, and the matcher allows nothing, so the request ends with empty output.

**Why `validation_error`.** It is the existing "the request itself is invalid" signal on `RequestError`, and Python's `to_exception` already maps it to 400; a compile failure of the request's own constraint is the same kind of error. Python's frontend validation already returns 400 for these constraints when it can check them, so this only changes requests that reach the engine unvalidated. The Rust side adds `RequestError::VALIDATION_ERROR` and `is_validation_error()` next to the existing `retryable` handling rather than an enum: `code` is an open string on the Python side, and no other code needs distinct Rust behavior.

**Not changed.**
- A streaming request still gets HTTP 200 with an SSE error event, as with Python, since compilation finishes after the response starts.
- xgrammar error messages include its log prefix (`[time] /project/cpp/...:line:`). Python's HTTP layer rewrites such paths with `sanitize_message`; the Rust frontend passes the message through.

**Not a duplicate.**
- #49625 (merged) rejects backend mismatches before compilation; this PR reports compilation failures with the same code.
- #45012 (open, inactive since 2026-08-19) handles failed grammar futures leaving requests blocked and reports them through the internal-error path (500); #47312 has since fixed the hang. This PR changes the status of those failures to 400.
- vllm-project/vllm#62456 (open) gives every Rust route one backend, which removes the mismatch case for the Rust frontend; the two PRs are independent.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Fix Gemma 4 image/audio placeholder strings
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #61195. `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.get_placeholder_str` returned Gemma 3n's `<image_soft_token>` / `<audio_soft_token>`, so with `--chat-template-content-format string` every Gemma 4 image or audio chat request failed with `Failed to apply prompt replacement`. It now returns `<|image|>` / `<|audio|>`, the tokens the prompt replacements target.

## Claims

- Gemma 4 image and audio chat requests work with `--chat-template-content-format string` instead of returning HTTP 500.
- `DiffusionGemmaForConditionalGeneration`, which registers Gemma 4's multimodal processor, gets the same image fix. `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` inherits the Gemma 4 method and is covered without a change.
- No change for the default `openai` content format: there the chat template inserts `<|image|>` itself, and `get_placeholder_str` never reaches the prompt text.

## Validation

New test `test_placeholder_str_is_replaced` in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py`. It resolves the model class the way the chat frontend does (`get_model_cls`), writes its `get_placeholder_str` into a prompt, and runs the real multimodal processor (configs and tokenizer only, no weights).

| Case | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, image | `Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][0]` | passed |
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, audio | `Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['audio'][0]` | passed |
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, video | passed | passed |
| `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it`, image | `Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][0]` | passed |
| `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it`, video | passed | passed |

Commands, run on macOS arm64 with CPU only. vLLM was imported from the source tree without compiled extensions, so `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu` selects the CPU platform:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py \
  tests/renderers/test_gemma4_chat_template.py
# 55 passed, 19 skipped (the skips are test_gemma4_unified.py: checkpoint marked not available online)

pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/diffusion_gemma.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4.py
# all hooks pass
```

Through the chat frontend: `parse_chat_messages(..., content_format="string")`, then the Gemma 4 chat template, then the processor, with `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` and one image + text user message:

- Before: content is `'<image_soft_token>\nWhat is in this image?'`, and processing fails with `AssertionError: Failed to apply prompt replacement for mm_items['image'][0]`.
- After: content is `'<|image|>\nWhat is in this image?'`, and the image placeholder lands at offset 4 with length 258, the same as with the `openai` format. The two rendered prompts differ only by the `\n` that the string path puts between content parts.

Not tested: a GPU server run of this branch, and model evals. The original failure came from `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.24.0` serving a Gemma 4 31B instruction model, and this machine has no GPU.

## Details

Root cause (full write-up in #61195):

- `_get_prompt_updates` targets the HF processor's `image_token_id` / `audio_token_id`. In Gemma 4's `tokenizer_config.json` these are `<|image|>` (258880) and `<|audio|>` (258881), and the chat template emits the same tokens.
- `<image_soft_token>` / `<audio_soft_token>` are the Gemma 3n strings (`gemma3n_mm.py`) and are not in Gemma 4's vocabulary.
- In the `string` content format, `MultiModalItemTracker.add` returns `get_placeholder_str(...)`, and `_get_full_multimodal_text_prompt` writes it into the message text. So the replacement target never appears in the prompt.

`get_placeholder_str` is a classmethod with no processor access, so the fix keeps the hard-coded strings that `gemma3_mm.py`, `gemma3n_mm.py` and the existing Gemma 4 `"<|video|>"` branch use. The Gemma 4 offline example (`examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py`) and the Rust frontend's Gemma 4 spec in #58649 already use `<|image|>`.

Why this is not a duplicate: I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `image_soft_token`, `get_placeholder_str` + Gemma 4, `Failed to apply prompt replacement`, and Gemma 4 + content format. #41452 / #41459 fixed the same error message for images in tool messages, which has a different cause (the tool-message template). The follow-on `Expected a cached item for mm_hash` error described in #61195 is the general cache desync tracked in #46354 and is not addressed here.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the fix and test, and draft this description. The commit carries a `Co-Authored-By` trailer.

commits.pr_title: Fix torchcodec lazy-import startup crash when native lib raises OSError
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Widens the module-scope torchcodec import guard in `vllm/multimodal/media/audio.py` to also catch `OSError`, so `vllm serve` starts cleanly even when torchcodec's bundled native library fails to load (e.g. built against a CUDA runtime that is not installed). Fixes #60406.

## Claims

- `vllm serve` no longer dies at import time when `torch.ops.load_library` inside torchcodec raises `OSError`.
- With torchcodec unavailable, `AudioDecoder` is `None` and `load_audio(backend='auto')` falls back to soundfile/PyAV instead of crashing.
- The original `OSError` is preserved in `_torchcodec_import_exc` and chained into the deferred `ImportError`, so the real cause is not hidden.

## Validation

The full vLLM test suite is not runnable in this environment (needs CUDA + full install). I verified with a harness driving the real fixed `audio.py` with heavy deps stubbed and a fake torchcodec whose `decoders/__init__.py` raises `OSError` at import (faithful to the issue): 9/9 checks passed — fixed module imports cleanly, `AudioDecoder` is `None`, the `OSError` is preserved and chained into the deferred `ImportError`, the healthy-torchcodec control is unaffected, and the pre-fix file demonstrably crashes with `OSError` on import.

## Details

Root cause: torchcodec 0.17.0's bundled native lib (built against CUDA 13) fails inside `torch.ops.load_library`, which raises `OSError` (torch/_ops.py). The existing guard caught only `(ImportError, RuntimeError)`, so the `OSError` propagated and killed the whole `vllm serve` startup path even for text-only serving. The fix is a one-line widening of the except clause plus a comment citing the issue. No new third-party APIs are called; `requirements/cuda.txt` already pins `torchcodec >= 0.14` unbounded, matching the issue's analysis.

commits.pr_title: [Model][LoRA] Enable LoRA support for BERT cross-encoders
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enable LoRA for `BertForSequenceClassification` cross-encoders, e.g. `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2`. That includes PEFT `SEQ_CLS` adapters that save a trained classification head. Follow-up to #61033 (BERT/RoBERTa embedding models); same pattern as #58884.

## Claims

- `--enable-lora` works instead of failing with `... does not support LoRA yet.`
- PEFT adapters with a saved head (`modules_to_save=["classifier"]`) load and match transformers + PEFT. Backbone-only adapters match too.
- Without LoRA, outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

Tesla T4, main @ e0317b28c. Random PEFT adapters (r=8, `init_lora_weights=False`); saved heads are perturbed so they differ from the base head. Each pair is scored with `LLM.score`, vLLM fp16 vs transformers + PEFT (merged) fp32 on CPU, 4 query/document pairs.

| Model | Adapter | Max abs diff, base | Max abs diff, LoRA vs HF+PEFT | LoRA effect (HF) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 (raw logits) | encoder q/k/v/dense + saved head | 0.0022 | 0.0027 | 13.53 |
| ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 (raw logits) | encoder q/k/v/dense only | 0.0022 | 0.0110 | 7.25 |

- **On main:** the model fails at startup with `... does not support LoRA yet.`
- **With only `SupportsLoRA` added (no classifier change):** the saved-head adapter fails with `ValueError: Cannot load full module 'classifier': the model does not expose a unique ClassificationHeadWithLoRA.`
- **Existing tests,** each passing both before and after the change:
  - `tests/models/language/pooling/test_classification.py::test_bert_model_runner_v2`
  - `tests/models/test_registry.py`
  - `tests/models/test_initialization.py -k BertForSequenceClassification`
  - `tests/lora/test_sequence_classification.py`
  - `tests/models/language/pooling_mteb_test/test_cross_encoder.py`

The comparison script (adapter generation + vLLM vs HF+PEFT check) is ~150 lines; happy to share it or turn it into a `tests/lora` case if useful.

## Details

- **`classifier`: `nn.Linear` → `ReplicatedLinear(..., return_bias=False)`.** With the default `target_modules`, `LoRAModelManager` only wraps `LinearBase` modules (`is_supported_lora_module`). A plain `nn.Linear` classifier therefore never becomes a `ClassificationHeadWithLoRA`, and `_validate_modules_to_save` rejects saved heads. This matches how `as_seq_cls_model` builds `score`, and #60211 makes the same change for RoBERTa's head. BERT's head is a single linear, so this stays within the existing single-layer `modules_to_save` contract. Same weights, bias and `head_dtype`, so non-LoRA outputs are identical. The weight names are unchanged.
- **`packed_modules_mapping`:** `qkv_proj ← query/key/value`. BERT's vLLM module names already match HF, so no `hf_to_vllm_mapper` is needed.
- **`self.config`** is needed by the LoRA manager.
- **Limitation: `bert.pooler.dense` is not LoRA-wrapped,** because `BertPooler.dense` is a plain `nn.Linear`. An adapter that targets it loads and the pooler LoRA is dropped: max abs diff 0.42 vs HF on the pooler-targeting adapter. This is the same class of issue as RoBERTa's `classifier.dense` in #60211. Making it a `ReplicatedLinear` would apply token-indexed LoRA in a per-sequence stage, so I left it. Happy to follow the reviewers' preference: reject such adapters, or let BERT opt `bert.pooler.dense` in if `lora_classifier_modules` from #60211 lands.
- **ModernBERT left out on purpose:** #59206 moves `ModernBertForSequenceClassification` to the Transformers modeling backend and removes the native class, so I didn't touch it. The same change does work there (gte-reranker-modernbert-base on the same T4 setup: max abs diff 0.0002 with a saved head, 0.0014 encoder-only), and I'm happy to send it separately if that's useful before #59206 lands.
- **Scope and fallback:** this does not change `modules_to_save` or any shared LoRA code. It only makes this single-linear classifier eligible for the existing saved-head path. If maintainers prefer not to widen saved-head support for now (see the scope discussion on #60211), the `ReplicatedLinear` change can be dropped. That leaves backbone-only LoRA, as in #58884, which the "encoder only" rows above already validate.
- **No file overlap with #60211** (`vllm/lora/*`, `roberta.py`).
- **CI gap:** no new test. LoRA correctness needs a GPU and adapter checkpoints. Happy to add a `tests/lora` case if wanted.
