commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Match DeepSeek DSML markers by token identity
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make the Rust DeepSeek DSML tool parser (V3.2, V4, V4.1) treat the tool-calls and invoke markers as structure only when their `｜DSML｜` is the dedicated token, so DSML written with ordinary tokens stays text. Stacked on #62874, which passes attributed deltas and the tokenizer to tool parsers. The matching reasoning change for `</think>` is #62892, independent of this stack.

## Claims

- DSML written with ordinary tokens, for example the model explaining the format in its answer, no longer starts a tool call.
- Ordinary `</｜DSML｜invoke>` / `</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` inside a string argument no longer end the invoke early.
- An ordinary partial `<｜DS` streams immediately instead of being held back.
- Output with the dedicated token parses exactly as before. DeepSeek V3.2-Exp, whose tokenizer has no `｜DSML｜` token, keeps matching by spelling.

## Validation

From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo nextest run --workspace --features vllm-parser/test-util --no-fail-fast   # 2234 passed, 13 skipped
cargo clippy -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets --features vllm-parser/test-util -- -D warnings
cargo bench -p vllm-parser --features test-util --bench deepseek_v32 -- reuse_parser
```

- **New regression tests** (`tool/deepseek_dsml/deepseek_v4.rs`) feed token IDs through the real incremental decoder, mixing dedicated and ordinary encodings: an ordinary DSML call stays text; ordinary invoke and tool-calls closers inside a string value stay in the value; an ordinary partial `<｜DS` streams immediately; a dedicated call split at every char boundary (including right after the `<` and inside the `｜DSML｜` spelling) still parses; a tokenizer without `｜DSML｜` parses by spelling. The existing DSML suites (V3.2, V4, V4.1) now run on attributed input and pass unchanged.
- **Fails before the fix.** The new tests use the attributed APIs from #62874 and this PR, so they do not compile on `main`; the equivalent check removes only the guard (build the markers with `then_text` instead of `then_special`):

  ```text
  $ cargo nextest run -p vllm-parser --features test-util deepseek_v4
  FAIL tool::deepseek_dsml::deepseek_v4::tests::deepseek_v4_ordinary_partial_tool_calls_marker_streams_immediately
  FAIL tool::deepseek_dsml::deepseek_v4::tests::deepseek_v4_ordinary_tool_calls_marker_stays_text
       left: "Write "   right: "Write <｜DSML｜tool_calls>\n<｜DSML｜invoke name=\"get_weather\">…</｜DSML｜tool_calls> here."
  FAIL tool::deepseek_dsml::deepseek_v4::tests::deepseek_v4_ordinary_block_closers_inside_parameter_value_stay_value
  Summary 14 tests run: 11 passed, 3 failed
  ```

  With the guard, all 14 pass.
- **End to end with real tokenizers:** `roundtrip_deepseek_v4`, `roundtrip_deepseek_v41` and `roundtrip_deepseek_v32` in `rust/src/chat/tests/roundtrip.rs` render with the native renderer, tokenize with the real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` and `DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp` tokenizers, decode through the production decoder and parse the tool calls: V4 and V4.1 through the guarded markers, V3.2-Exp through the spelling fallback.
- **Benchmark** (`deepseek_v32`, `reuse_parser`, single runs on a shared host):

  | Fixture | `main` (text-only, plain chunks) | this PR, spelling fallback | this PR, guarded |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | mixed text + 2 calls | 8.95 µs | 22.0 µs | 21.2 µs |
  | long normal text (135 KB) | 1.15 ms | 3.69 ms | 3.41 ms |

  The guard itself costs nothing measurable; the gap to `main` is carrying one attribution per token in the buffer. The test tokenizer is byte-level, so these fixtures carry one attribution per byte, about four times what a real BPE tokenizer produces. The bench now feeds attributed chunks from a tokenizer with `｜DSML｜`, as the Kimi K3 bench does; otherwise it would silently measure the fallback.
- No GPU serving run or accuracy eval. With the dedicated token, parser output is unchanged (existing suites and the real-tokenizer roundtrips pass); only ordinary-token spellings of the markers behave differently.

## Details

- **Root cause:** the parser matched every marker with `literal` / `take_until` on decoded text, so it could not tell the dedicated `｜DSML｜` token from the same bytes spelled by ordinary tokens.
- **Markers:** in every DSML marker only `｜DSML｜` is an added token (V4/V4.1 id 128825, `special=false`; V3.2 id 128793, `special=true`); `<`, `tool_calls>`, `invoke`, `parameter` are ordinary pieces. Each marker is therefore `Marker::text("<").then_special(｜DSML｜).then_text("tool_calls>")`: the guard sits mid-marker, candidates come from text occurrences, and the identity check happens when the marker is parsed. This reuses the Kimi K3 `Marker` / `MarkerStream` utilities from #58358; no new utility types.
- **Parsing:** the buffer is a `DecodedText` parsed with `parse_buffered_event_attributed`. The invoke closer is found with `take_until_marker` on the streaming buffer, so an ordinary closer inside a value no longer ends the invoke.
- **Fallback:** when the tokenizer lacks `｜DSML｜` (DeepSeek V3.2-Exp spells DSML with ordinary tokens), the markers fall back to spelling.
- **Why token identity:** DeepSeek's own streaming output parser matches these markers the same way: it splits each marker into plain and special segments and lets special segments match only bytes decoded from the added token ([deepseek-recipe `output_parser.rs`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe/blob/935817c66f5d6e64838f419692545f06787e485f/deepseek-recipe/src/stream/output_parser.rs#L338-L408)).
- **Known limitation, parameters:** as for the Kimi K3 call body in #58358, a complete invoke body is still parsed from text, so an ordinary `</｜DSML｜parameter>` inside a string value still ends the value. Guarding parameter markers needs an attributed view of a complete body; that interface is left to a follow-up shared with the K3 call body. Keeping parameters text-matched also agrees with the output grammar, whose `deepseek_xml` argument style constrains parameter markers by text.
- **Known limitation, grammar:** the tool-call structural tags still constrain DSML by text. Under `tool_choice=required`, a named function or `strict` tools, a grammar-forced tool-calls or invoke marker spelled with ordinary tokens would be accepted by XGrammar but read as text by the parser. The model strongly prefers the dedicated token, so this is unlikely, but it is silent. XGrammar 0.2.7 can express token-level boundaries (`Token` in sequences, `token_dispatch`); that is a separate change.

Not a duplicate: the open DeepSeek DSML PRs (#62517, #62259, #54686, #58322, #61142) change the Python parsers or the tokenizer encoding. #62290 changes the same Rust DSML parser to drop an incomplete call at `max_tokens`; it is a different behavior, and whichever lands second needs a rebase.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Pass attributed deltas and the tokenizer to tool parsers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Give Rust tool parsers what a token-aware parser needs: `ToolParser::parse_into` takes the attributed `DecodedText` delta instead of `&str`, and `ToolParser::create` receives the model tokenizer. Behavior-preserving; the bottom of a stack whose next PR makes the DeepSeek DSML tool parser match its markers by token identity.

## Claims

- `ToolParser::parse_into(&mut self, chunk: DecodedText, ..)`, as `ReasoningParser::push` and `UnifiedParser::parse_into` already are. `CombinedParser` passes reasoning content through with its attribution instead of dropping it to `content.text`.
- `ToolParser::create(tools, tokenizer)` and the chat `ToolParserFactory`, so a parser can resolve its marker token IDs once at construction, as reasoning and unified parsers do.
- No parser output changes: every existing tool parser matches by spelling and reads only `chunk.text`, and none reads the tokenizer yet.

## Validation

From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo nextest run --workspace --features vllm-parser/test-util --no-fail-fast
cargo clippy -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets --features vllm-parser/test-util -- -D warnings
```

The workspace suite passes unchanged apart from call-site updates (the `parse_chunk` / `collect_stream` test helpers keep their `&str` inputs and wrap them as unattributed text), and Clippy is clean. Pure interface change, so no new tests.

## Details

- Why: a tool parser cannot tell a dedicated marker token from an ordinary-token spelling of the same bytes while the trait hands it plain text, and it has no tokenizer to learn the marker's token ID. Unified parsers (Kimi K3) already have both.
- Changing the signature in one pass rather than adding a defaulted `parse_decoded_into` keeps one entry point, matching how `ReasoningParser::push` and `UnifiedParser::parse_into` were migrated. The diff is mechanical: one line per parser plus imports and test call sites.
- `reset() -> String` is unchanged: recovery does not need attribution.
- Two commits: the delta type and the tokenizer argument.

Not a duplicate: the open DSML PRs (#62517, #62259, #54686, #58322) change the Python parsers or tokenizer encoding; none touches the Rust `ToolParser` trait.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EPD] Check encoder readiness for prefix replay
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Wait for encoder embeddings needed by prefix replay before admitting an EPD request.

## Claims

- Include the replayed prefix tail in EC readiness checks without changing KV-hit accounting or replay behavior when a KV load restores the window.
- Prevent missing encoder embeddings from crashing the consumer during DeepSeek-V4.1 prefix replay.

## Validation

Slurm E2E: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1E (TP1) + 1PD (TP2), Mooncake TCP, MRV2, raw-image forwarding, prefix/processor caches and CUDA Graphs enabled. After 128 disjoint random-image warmups, MUIRBench (512 questions, concurrency 64) completed with **512/512 HTTP 200**, **303/512 correct (59.18%)**, and no `Encoder cache miss`, using an 8 GiB consumer pool.

## Details

EC readiness was checked before SWA replay rewound the computed-token boundary. For example, a KV hit at 640 covers an image ending at 567, but replay starts at 512 and still needs that image. Skipping its load causes `Encoder cache miss`. Check EC readiness against the replay start while retaining the original KV-hit boundary for allocation and statistics.

Checked related open EPD/prefix-replay PRs; none addresses this missing-load path. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][Pooling] Serve late chunking through /v1/embeddings
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add token embeddings and optional late chunking to `/v1/embeddings` and `LLM.embed`. This is the embedding entrypoint alternative to #61419, requested for comparison in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61419#issuecomment-6161948029. It uses the core from #60164 and RFC #58774.

## Claims

- With the `token_embed` task, both entrypoints return token vectors by default and chunk vectors when `late_chunking_params` is set.
- Chunk results include token and source ranges. The offline example uses `LLM.embed`; `LLM.encode` remains available.
- ORJSON responses reuse the existing ndarray encoder. Ordinary `embed` output and the `/pooling` schemas are unchanged.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| CPU protocol, metadata, routing and output suites | 87 passed |
| E5 token embedding HTTP suite | 18 passed with each runner |
| E5 token embedding offline checks | 10 passed with each runner |
| Existing ordinary embedding offline and HTTP checks | 8 and 3 passed |
| Updated offline example | Prints chunk vectors and source ranges for both documents |

GPU checks use an A100 80GB and `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small` at revision `614241f622f53c4eeff9890bdc4f31cfecc418b3`. The HTTP suite uses bfloat16 and a 512 token context. It checks ordinary token vectors against `/pooling`, chunk means against contextual token vectors, source offsets, concurrent requests and invalid inputs. These are correctness checks, not retrieval quality benchmarks.

GPU checks predate the final offline validation adjustment, which is covered by CPU tests. Model computation and HTTP handling are unchanged by that adjustment. The CPU suite was rerun after syncing with main and moving the test file: 87 passed.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_factories.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/test_utils.py tests/test_outputs.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py

for runner in 1 0; do
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=$runner .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
    tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_online.py
  VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=$runner .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
    tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_offline.py \
    -k 'test_str_prompts or test_token_ids_prompts or test_e5_late_chunking_mixed_requests or test_unsupported_tasks'
done
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_offline.py
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_online.py \
  -k 'test_basic or test_pooling_embed or test_use_activation'
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 .venv/bin/python \
  examples/pooling/token_embed/late_chunking_offline.py --chunk-size 16
```

</details>

## Details

The handler reuses `TokenEmbedIOProcessor` and the existing chunk implementation. Route registration selects the schema for the configured task. Missing or null chunk parameters select ordinary token embeddings; malformed chunk parameters remain errors.

For offline `token_embed`, `LLM.embed` returns the existing `PoolingRequestOutput`, preserving its tensor matrix and chunk metadata. The `embed` task keeps its `EmbeddingRequestOutput` conversion. Existing `LLM.encode` validation rejects unsupported tasks and retains its configuration guidance.

For ColBERT, `LLM.embed` now returns token vectors instead of raising. Explicitly requesting `pooling_task="embed"` remains unsupported, which the updated ColBERT test checks. This does not change which models support late chunking.

The HTTP matrix-valued `embedding` and optional `late_chunking` metadata are a vLLM extension. Only float encoding is supported. Chunking requires plain text; ordinary token embeddings also accept token IDs. Ordinary `embed` servers do not enable chunking and can ignore an unrecognized `late_chunking_params` field. Cohere `/v2/embed`, the batch API and `/invocations` are not extended with chunking. On `token_embed` servers, `/v2/embed` is not registered, changing its unsupported API response from 501 to 404 for models advertising both tasks.

commits.pr_title: [Core][Sleep Mode] Use torch.accelerator in CuMemAllocator free/sleep
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Finish the supported `torch.accelerator` migration in `vllm/device_allocator/cumem.py` (RFC #30679) by replacing the last two generic `torch.cuda` calls:

- `_python_free_callback()`: `torch.cuda.synchronize(data.handle[0])` -> `torch.accelerator.synchronize(data.handle[0])`
- `sleep()`: `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` -> `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()`

The CUDA-specific allocator APIs (`CUDAPluggableAllocator`, `MemPool`, `use_mem_pool`, `cudaMemcpy`/`cudaMemset`, `CudaRTLibrary`, and the cuMem C extension) are intentionally unchanged, as are `get_pluggable_allocator()`, `use_memory_pool_with_allocator()`, `cudagraph_pool()`, and `_trim()`.

Status: open for human review; the submitting human should review every changed line before merge.

## Claims

- The two remaining generic calls in `cumem.py` now dispatch through `torch.accelerator`; the device index and call positions are preserved.
- No CUDA/ROCm behavior change: the free path still synchronizes before returning the handle (and before the C extension unmaps), the ROCm already-asleep short-circuit still returns an empty chunk list without an extra sync, and `sleep()` still clears the cache once after `gc.collect()`.
- Hardens the existing `test_basic_cumem` case instead of adding a test file: it records `torch.accelerator.empty_cache` around `sleep()` and `torch.accelerator.synchronize` around a freed cuMem allocation, asserting the cache is emptied once and the free callback synchronizes the allocation's device index.
- Updates the `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` comment in `use_memory_pool()` to the unified API while retaining the PyTorch issue references.
- No new dependency, no public API change, no C++/CUDA change.

## Validation

CI coverage: `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py` is run by `basic-correctness-cumem` (`pytest -v -s basic_correctness/memory/cumem`) on CUDA and ROCm.

The branch includes a merge of main at `e632d66433`; the H20 run used the per-commit wheel built for that merge base.

H20 (SGP cluster) job `1394`, node `vllm-sgp-h20-01`, 1x NVIDIA H20-3e, torch 2.13.0+cu130, vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev185+ge632d6643` from the per-commit wheel, with the PR's `cumem.py` and `test_cumem.py` overlaid:

| Area | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU cuMem tests | `pytest -q --import-mode=importlib tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py -v -k "test_basic_cumem or test_discard_tags or test_reentered_tag or test_cumem_with_cudagraph or test_cudagraph_pool_sleep"` | **7 passed**, 14 deselected, in 14.05s |

The 7 GPU cases are `test_basic_cumem`, `test_discard_tags`, `test_reentered_tag[x-freed]`, `test_reentered_tag[x-alive]`, `test_cumem_with_cudagraph`, and `test_cudagraph_pool_sleep[sleep-1]` / `[sleep-2]`. `test_basic_cumem` now also checks the two migrated accelerator calls; the others cover the allocator sleep/wake paths, tag-selective discard, re-entered tags, and CUDA Graph pool backup/restore.

Pre-commit on the head node (shared hook cache):

```text
bash $HOME/vllm-shared/scripts/run-precommit.sh <worktree> e8e1e96196725f097eae2394cbc458b1f5a679b8
ruff check ... Passed
ruff format ... Passed
typos ... Passed
check-test-tethering ... Passed
mypy ... Passed
check-spdx-header ... Passed
check-torch-cuda-call ... Passed
DCO check ... ok
```

Not verified: ROCm hardware (no ROCm node available; the hardened test runs in the ROCm `basic-correctness-cumem` CI job), and the 14 model-dependent cases in `test_cumem.py` that start `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (not needed for an API-only swap). Full Buildkite CI has not been run on this head; the existing build targets the previous merge commit.

## Details

- `torch.accelerator.synchronize(device)` forwards the device index exactly as `torch.cuda.synchronize(device)` did. The existing `data.is_asleep and current_platform.is_rocm()` return stays before the sync, so already-unmapped allocations still skip it.
- `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` still runs after `gc.collect()`, so cache cleanup order and the allocator's offload/discard bookkeeping are unchanged.
- `test_basic_cumem` wraps the accelerator entry points; a revert to a non-accelerator call leaves the recorded calls empty and fails the test. It does not mock private methods or log order.
- `torch.accelerator.synchronize` is used in `discard()` and `wake_up()` already; this change removes the remaining generic calls without touching them.
- Why not duplicate: searched open PRs for `cumem`, `device_allocator`, and `torch.accelerator`; none covers these two calls. #59523 migrated the other calls in this file and is merged.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Move 1-byte expert tensors as uint8 views
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51567.

When EPLB is enabled, expert tensors whose dtype NCCL does not support make engine startup fail. MXFP4 and MXFP8 experts store block scales as `torch.float8_e8m0fnu`. ROCm AITER MXFP4 also views expert weights as `torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2`. Neither dtype exists in NCCL or RCCL.

I hit this with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash using MXFP4 experts (Humming MoE backend), TP8 + EP + EPLB, on 8x H20. The crash happens in the first rearrange during memory profiling.

With `communicator=torch_nccl`:

```text
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 572, in determine_available_memory
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/eplb_utils.py", line 126, in step
File "vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_state.py", line 580, in step
...
File "torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py", line 4280, in all_gather
    work = group.allgather([tensor_list], [tensor], opts)
TypeError: Input tensor data type is not supported for NCCL process group: Float8_e8m0fnu
```

With `communicator=pynccl`:

```text
File "vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py", line 756, in create_eplb_communicator
    return _create_pynccl()
File "vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py", line 693, in _create_pynccl
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: EPLB communicator 'pynccl' requested but expert weights contain unsupported dtypes: (torch.float8_e8m0fnu).
```

## When this triggers

The bug is not tied to a specific model architecture. It depends on the dtype that the MoE backend leaves in the expert parameters after weight post-processing. Startup fails when all of these hold:

1. EPLB is enabled (`--enable-eplb`, with EP).
2. The experts use MX quantization (MXFP4/MXFP8 with E8M0 block scales).
3. After post-processing, the backend stores an expert tensor in a 1-byte dtype that NCCL/RCCL does not support. For example:
   - Marlin MXFP4 MoE: `mxfp4_marlin_process_scales()` returns scales as `float8_e8m0fnu`.
   - ROCm AITER MXFP4: expert weights are viewed as `float4_e2m1fn_x2` (`oracle/mxfp4.py`).
   - Humming MXFP4 (my repro): scales are stored as `float8_e8m0fnu`.

   Backends that keep these tensors as `uint8` are not affected.
4. The tensor is returned by `get_expert_weights()`, so it is registered for EPLB transport.

Converting at load time is not enough. DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 loaders already view checkpoint E8M0 scales as `uint8`, but the backend's kernel-format conversion writes `float8_e8m0fnu` back into the parameter. The fix therefore belongs where the tensors are registered for EPLB, not in individual loaders or backends.

## Root cause

EPLB treats expert tensors as opaque payload. It only sends, receives, and all-gathers them, and never reduces them. However, it passes their numeric dtype straight to the communicator. On the first rearrange (the dummy all-gather during `determine_available_memory`), the communicator has to map that dtype to an NCCL dtype. NCCL only supports `int8/uint8/int32/int64/fp16/fp32/fp64/bf16` and FP8 E4M3/E5M2, so the mapping fails:

- `torch_nccl` raises `TypeError` inside `all_gather`.
- `pynccl` rejects the dtype earlier, when the communicator is created.

## Fix

EPLB only copies expert bytes between ranks. It never reduces them, so the numeric dtype does not matter to the transport. In `MixtureOfExperts.set_eplb_state()`, every 1-byte expert tensor is now registered as `w.view(torch.uint8)`:

- The view keeps the shape, stride, and storage, so a rearrange writes directly into the parameter that the kernels read in the original dtype.
- Applying the view at this registration point covers `FusedMoE` layers, models with their own `get_expert_weights()` (for example DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE), and elastic EP re-registration.
- 1-byte dtypes that NCCL already supports (`int8`, `uint8`, `float8_e4m3fn`) move the same bytes as before.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py -k byte_dtypes -v
pre-commit run --files tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py
```

## Test Result

**Unit test:** the new test is parametrized over `float8_e8m0fnu` and `float4_e2m1fn_x2`. Both cases pass with this change and fail on `main`. pre-commit (ruff, mypy) passes.

**MXFP4 deployment with EPLB (8x H20, SM90):** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with MXFP4 experts, Humming MoE backend (`HummingIndexedExperts`), TP8 + EP + EPLB (sync, `pynccl`, 16 redundant experts, `step_interval=1500`). The image is `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` with this PR's diff applied to `interfaces.py`. On this setup, startup previously failed with the tracebacks above.

- Startup: the profile rearrange passes and the server starts.
  ```text
  Rearranging experts sync mode (profile)...
  Rearranged experts  (profile)  in 2.30 s.
  Application startup complete.
  ```
- Real rearranges: three ran during the GSM8K run below. The first took 6.64 s and the next two took 0.27 s each. Balancedness was about 0.70 before the first rearrange and 0.82 to 0.87 after.
- Accuracy across rearranges (GSM8K, all 1319 questions, 5-shot chat, concurrency 32): flex-extract 89.92% ± 0.83 (1186/1319). This matches our production deployment of the same model without EPLB (90.1%). All 8 smoke prompts were also answered correctly.
- None of the 8 ranks logged `Traceback`, `Float8_e8m0fnu`, `unsupported dtypes`, or `TypeError`.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Skip no-LoRA tokens (index -1) in CPU torch bgmv ops
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`token_lora_indices` marks base-model (no-LoRA) tokens with the sentinel `-1`
(see `PunicaWrapperBase`; the value is documented as "an index of -1 means no
lora should be applied"). The Triton LoRA kernels honor it by early-exiting
(`if lora_id == -1: return` in `lora_shrink_op`/`lora_expand_op`).

The pure-PyTorch fallback ops used on the **CPU platform**
(`vllm/lora/ops/torch_ops/lora_ops.py`) instead did:

```python
selected_loras = lora_b_weights[lora_indices_tensor]
```

For a `-1` token this selects `lora_b_weights[-1]` — the **last stacked
adapter** — instead of skipping. So in a mixed batch (e.g. the default
`max_loras=1` with one adapter loaded), a base-model request batched next to a
LoRA request silently gets the adapter's delta applied to its logits /
embeddings — wrong output, no error. This affects `bgmv_shrink`, `bgmv_expand`
and `bgmv_expand_slice`, and therefore the `sgmv_*` prefill ops that delegate to
them.

**Fix:** clamp the gather index to `0` and zero the LoRA delta for `-1` tokens
(`masked_fill`), mirroring the Triton early-exit. For valid indices the behavior
is bit-for-bit unchanged (`clamp` is a no-op, the mask is all-False), so the
existing kernel-parity tests are unaffected.

## Test Plan

Added `test_torch_ops_bgmv_skips_no_lora_tokens` to
`tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py`: a 2-token batch `[LoRA-0, no-LoRA(-1)]` run
through `bgmv_shrink` / `bgmv_expand` / `bgmv_expand_slice`, asserting the `-1`
token receives a zero delta and the valid token receives the correct delta.

```bash
pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py::test_torch_ops_bgmv_skips_no_lora_tokens
pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py       # full parity suite, no regressions
```

## Test Result

Verified on 1× NVIDIA H200 (torch 2.11.0).

```
# new test, BEFORE fix (base-model token wrongly modified):
>   assert torch.count_nonzero(y[1]) == 0
E   assert tensor(4) == 0
1 failed

# new test, AFTER fix:
1 passed

# full file (torch-vs-triton parity tests), AFTER fix:
4274 passed
```

`pre-commit run --files ...` (ruff, ruff-format, mypy, typos, SPDX) passes.

---

*AI assistance (Claude) was used to develop this change. The submitter has
reviewed every changed line and run the tests above.*

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Disable shared-expert aux stream with fully-sharded LoRA
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60845.

With `--fully-sharded-loras`, the shared experts' LoRA layers all-gather / all-reduce across TP, and the routed experts' fused MoE LoRA kernel does its own collectives on the main stream. Running the shared experts on the aux stream puts two collectives in flight on the same communicator. Under CUDA graph capture they become independent graph branches, and the replay order is not guaranteed to match across ranks, so NCCL deadlocks (first LoRA decode step hangs, then `RPC call to sample_tokens timed out`).

This PR runs the shared experts on the main stream when fully-sharded LoRA is enabled, same as the existing EPLB / flashinfer exclusions in `SharedExperts._disable_shared_experts_overlap`.

## Test Plan

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, TP=2, `--enable-lora --fully-sharded-loras --max-lora-rank 32`, default CUDA graphs, two rank-32 adapters alternating.

- v0.28.0 (reproduces the hang on the first LoRA request): with this patch, first request returns in 1s, 1000/1000 requests OK.
- v0.31.0 / main: 1000/1000 requests OK.

## Test Result

No hang, 0 failed in both runs.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Count unscheduled running requests toward max_loras
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Count the LoRA adapters of all running requests, not only those scheduled in the current step, when deciding whether a waiting request fits within `max_loras`. Without this, a skipped running request lets a request with another adapter in, and the next batch holds more than `max_loras` adapters and trips an assertion in `Scheduler.schedule()`.

Fixes #60301

## Claims

- With `--max-loras N`, a waiting request whose adapter would exceed `N` once a currently skipped running request resumes is no longer admitted early. This happens with pipeline parallelism and also on a single GPU, e.g. when a multimodal request is skipped because the step's encoder budget is used up.
- Fixes `AssertionError` in `schedule()` (`assert len(scheduled_loras) <= self.lora_config.max_loras`), which escapes the engine core busy loop and kills the engine.
- No behavior change when every running request is scheduled in the step.
- One-line source change (the iterable the set is built from) plus its comment; `create_scheduler` in the scheduler test helpers gains a `lora_config` argument.

## Validation

Repro on `main` (`bf049ddb8f`), CPU, `Scheduler` with `max_loras=1`, stepping `schedule()` and `update_from_output()` the way a pipeline-parallel engine does (a step's output returns only after the next `schedule()`):

1. `r1` (LoRA 1, 8-token prompt) is scheduled; its output is still in flight.
2. `r2` (LoRA 2) arrives. `r1` has nothing to run in step 2, so `scheduled_loras` is empty and `r2` is admitted.
3. `r1`'s output returns. Step 3 schedules `r1` (decode) and `r2` (next prefill chunk) together.

Before:

```
max_loras: 1
step1: {'r1': 8}
step2: {'r2': 16} running: ['r1', 'r2']
  File ".../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 877, in schedule
    assert len(scheduled_loras) <= self.lora_config.max_loras
AssertionError
```

After:

```
max_loras: 1
step1: {'r1': 8}
step2: {} running: ['r1']
step3: {'r1': 1}
distinct LoRAs in batch: {1} max_loras: 1
```

Randomized check (12 requests with LoRA ids drawn from {none, 1, 2, 3, 4}, random prompt lengths and arrival steps, `max_loras=2`, PP=2, `max_num_batched_tokens=16`, 200 seeds, requests complete after 4 tokens):

| | seeds finished | `AssertionError` in `schedule()` | max adapters in one batch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 176 | 24 | 2 |
| this PR | 200 | 0 | 2 |

Regression test `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_max_loras_counts_running_request_awaiting_output`:

```
# main
E       AssertionError: assert {'b': 8} == {}
E         Left contains 1 more item:
E         {'b': 8}
tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py:358: AssertionError
1 failed, 1 passed, 199 deselected

# this PR
tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_max_loras_counts_running_request_awaiting_output PASSED
```

Existing tests (CPU, `pytest -p no:cacheprovider`):

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
  45 failed, 175 passed
pytest tests/v1/core
  59 failed, 877 passed, 4 errors
```

All of these failures and errors are pre-existing: the same 59 test ids fail and the same 4 tests error on `main` (rerun there by node id). They are multimodal and e2e tests (`Llava`/`Qwen2.5-VL`/`Qwen3.5` architecture inspection fails, engine and server fixtures cannot start) in an environment without GPU or compiled kernels. None involve LoRA.

Re-checked after rebasing onto `e37e51dd24` (current `main`):

- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_max_loras_counts_running_request_awaiting_output` fails with `scheduler.py` reverted to `main` (`AssertionError: assert {'b': 8} == {}`) and passes with the fix.
- The scheduler-level repro in #60301 hits the assertion on `main` and runs to completion with this PR; the randomized check gives the same numbers as in the table (24 of 200 seeds fail on `main`, 0 with this PR).
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 343 passed, 46 failed. The same 46 tests fail on `main` (45 `LlavaForConditionalGeneration` inspection errors because `torchvision` is not installed here, 1 subprocess timeout in `test_kv_cache_utils.py`); none involve LoRA.
- `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/utils.py vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, which runs every hook CI runs (including `mypy` for Python 3.10 to 3.13): all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: `Scheduler.schedule()` seeds `scheduled_loras` from `scheduled_running_reqs` (`scheduler.py:869-877` on `main`) and the waiting loop admits a request only if its adapter fits in that set (`:918-929`). A running request is skipped in a step when it has nothing to schedule yet: with PP>1 once its prompt is fully scheduled but the output is pending (the `num_new_tokens == 0` case documented in the running loop), and through the other `continue` paths of the running loop (`next_decode_eligible_step` cadence for V2 + PP + async, DP prefill deferral, EC connector and encoder budget waits). Its adapter is then missing from the set, a request with another adapter is admitted, and once the skipped request is scheduled again both end up in one batch. The running loop does not consult `max_loras`, so the existing `assert` is the first thing to notice.

Fix: seed the set from `self.running`. Every request enters `self.running` through the waiting-loop admission check, so the number of distinct adapters among running requests stays at most `max_loras` and the assert holds. This is how the V0 scheduler counted (`curr_loras` was built from all running sequence groups), and what `LoRAConfig.max_loras` ("Max number of LoRAs in a single batch") requires. The variable keeps its name since it is still the set the waiting loop extends as it admits requests.

Scope and limits: the check is more conservative only when a running request that holds an adapter is skipped in the step; that request's adapter slot is kept until it finishes. Two tests cover it: the pipeline-parallel case and, without PP, a running request skipped because earlier requests used up the step's encoder compute budget (suggested in review). Both fail on `main` and pass with this change. Open priority-preemption PRs (#40087, #45558, #45561, #54530) read and update `scheduled_loras` but do not change how it is seeded.

Not a duplicate: I searched issues and PRs on `vllm-project/vllm` for `max_loras`, `scheduled_loras`, `LoRA scheduler`, `LoRA pipeline`, `LoRA async`, `max_loras assertion` and `no free lora slots`, and open PRs for `scheduler.py lora` and `LoRA schedule running requests`. Nothing reports or fixes this. Closest hits: #15422 (merged, introduced the current seeding), #14495 (closed feature request about "No free lora slots" for over-full batches, predates #15422), #17003 (usage question), #10840 (closed, a V0 LoRA scheduling policy), and the open priority-preemption PRs above.

This PR was co-authored with Claude.

End-to-end validation in review: on 2×H20 (Qwen3-0.6B, 3 LoRAs, PP=2, `max_loras=1`) `main` dies with `EngineDeadError` from this assert in all four MRV2/V1 × sync/async combinations and this PR completes with outputs matching per-request runs; the single-GPU encoder-budget case (Qwen3.5-4B, `max_loras=2`) reproduces and is fixed as well.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3] MonoKernel: serve EAGLE3 verify steps
commits.pr_body:
## Summary
`--monokernel` (MiniMax-M3 FFN MonoKernel, #62712) previously refused speculative decoding. The fused FFN launch is per-row and reads no KV cache, so EAGLE3 verify rows need only host-side changes:
- The config refusal accepts `eagle3` (all other spec methods are still refused).
- Routing drops the one-token-per-request checks: a decode step with <= 16 rows and no prefill runs fused (eager or FULL graph); larger or mixed steps run stock.
- The mono layer loop captures EAGLE3 aux hidden states.

No kernel changes and no core vLLM changes.

## Results (MI355X, TP4, MT-Bench, FULL graphs, EAGLE3 k=3)
Identical flags on both arms except `--monokernel`. Two interleaved rounds, which agreed within 0.04 ms.

| Concurrency | ITL p50 stock -> mono | Output tok/s stock -> mono | Acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.98 -> **6.11 ms (-12.5%)** | 383 -> **435 (+13.6%)** | 2.78 / 2.78 |
| 2 | 8.03 -> **7.25 ms (-9.7%)** | 617 -> **683 (+10.7%)** | 2.74 / 2.76 |
| 4 | 9.11 -> 9.01 ms (-1%) | 1019 -> 1028 (+0.9%) | 2.83 / 2.79 |

Above 4 requests (more than 16 verify rows), steps run stock, so behavior is unchanged.

GSM8K 5-shot (500 samples, paired): mono+EAGLE3 0.892 vs stock+EAGLE3 0.900 (-0.8 pp, 95% CI [-3.7, +2.1], McNemar p=0.69).

## Serve command
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1 \
vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --block-size 128 --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64]}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' --moe-backend aiter \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --monokernel   # omitted for the stock arm
```
Capture sizes in multiples of 4 are recommended: MRV2 rounds spec graph sizes to multiples of 4, so without 12, three requests pad to a 16-row graph.

## Benchmark command
```bash
vllm bench serve --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path philschmid/mt-bench --skip-chat-template \
  --hf-output-len 1024 --temperature 0 --seed 1234 \
  --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1   # c in {1, 2, 4}; num-prompts = max(16, 4*c)
```

## Tests
`tests/models/minimax_m3/amd_specialized_decode/`:
- New mini-model test (4 GPUs): EAGLE3 FULL-graph verify steps at 4/8/12/16 rows run fused and match native teacher-forced logprobs (cos 0.9991); a late rank fault during a verify step returns no token.
- Routing unit tests for q=4 at 4/8/12/16 rows (including padded rows); 20 rows, prefill and PIECEWISE steps route to stock.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Revert "[ROCm][Build] Compile paged attention kernels in parallel (7.6x faster attention build) (#62475)"
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reverts #62475 to unblock the ROCm 10.0 nightly while we pick a proper fix.

## Claims

- Fixes the `Build release image - x86_64 - ROCm 10.0` nightly failure: the `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link fails with `mold: relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against .eh_frame out of range`.

## Validation

Built and linked the full `_rocm_C` with this revert in the ROCm 10.0 CI build image (same compiler, mold, 9 release archs, `RelWithDebInfo`): link succeeds.

## Details

**Root cause:** `_rocm_C`'s embedded GPU code (`.hip_fatbin`) was already ~1.94 GiB, ~80% of it uncompressed GPU debug info. Splitting attention into 12 files duplicates that debug info per file and pushed the library past the 2 GiB relocation limit. This revert only gets us back under it, with ~64 MB of headroom.

**Alternatives** (each lets us reland #62475). Measured on one attention file, 9 archs:

| Option | GPU code size | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Today | 137 MiB | | |
| `-Xarch_device -g0` | 36 MiB (−74%) | Simple; ~20% faster compile | No GPU debug info (no kernel source debugging, no source lines for GPU faults) |
| `--offload-compress` | 4.9 MiB (−96%) | Keeps full debug info; output unchanged after decompression; smaller wheel | Decompression at module load (not yet measured on GPU); needs ROCm ≥ 6.2 |

Either option is a one-line CMake change. Both make every HIP object miss sccache once, so the next nightly after either lands is a cold build.

commits.pr_title: [Bench] Save server queue time and TTFT in detailed results
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
PR #46768 added server-side per-request timing metrics to OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Completions responses. However, `vllm bench serve` discarded these metrics and only retained client-observed timing data.

This PR preserves two server-side metrics in detailed benchmark results:

- `server_queue_times`: time spent waiting in the server scheduler queue.
- `server_ttfts`: time from scheduling to first-token generation.

Both values are converted from milliseconds to seconds to match the existing per-request benchmark arrays. Missing values are represented as `null` while preserving request-index alignment. Both arrays are omitted if neither metric is available for any request, or if --save-detailed is not enabled.

The implementation supports both the Python benchmark client and the Rust benchmark client used with `VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1`. Documentation is updated to distinguish these values from the client-side `queue_times` and `ttfts`.

This PR focuses on server-side queue time and TTFT to help **distinguish scheduler waiting time from time to first-token generation**. I’m happy to include the remaining per-request metrics if maintainers prefer a broader scope.

There is no associated issue. This is a follow-up integration to #46768.

I searched open PRs for `server_queue_times`, `server_ttfts`, and the combination of `enable-per-request-metrics` with `save-detailed`, and found no existing PR implementing this behavior.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used during implementation. I reviewed every changed line and can explain and maintain the change.

## Test Plan

- Verify that both Python Chat Completions and Completions clients extract metrics from the final streaming usage chunk.
- Verify millisecond-to-second conversion, zero-valued metrics, unavailable values, and per-request array alignment.
- Verify equivalent result serialization in the Rust benchmark client.
- Run the targeted Python and Rust tests.
- Run a Python end-to-end smoke test against a live `/v1/completions` endpoint
  and inspect the saved detailed JSON.


## Test Result

### Python targeted tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -v
```

Result: **27 passed, 14 warnings**. This includes the existing timing tests and the migrated server metrics tests.

### Rust targeted tests

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked -p vllm-bench server_metrics
```

Result: **5 passed, 0 failed**.

### Lint checks

Pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

### Python E2E smoke test

Behavior change:

- Before: detailed benchmark results did not contain server-side queue time
  or TTFT.
- After: detailed results include `server_queue_times` and `server_ttfts`
  when these metrics are available.

The smoke test was run on the modified version using
`gemma-4-E2B-it`, with `--enable-per-request-metrics`
enabled on the server:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --model /path/to/gemma-4-E2B-it \
  --dataset-name custom \
  --dataset-path toolagent_3k.jsonl \
  --num-prompts 3 \
  --disable-shuffle \
  --custom-output-len=-1 \
  --request-rate 0.6 \
  --save-result \
  --save-detailed \
  --result-dir results \
  --result-filename gemma4_server_metrics_smoke_3.json
```

Results:

- 3 successful requests, 0 failures.
- Both server timing arrays were present in the saved detailed JSON.
- Each array contained 3 non-null, non-negative values and matched the
  length of the existing per-request arrays.

Saved values, in seconds (rounded for readability):

```json
{
  "ttfts": [0.820385, 0.774362, 4.330024],
  "server_queue_times": [0.000060141, 0.000023473, 0.000028463],
  "server_ttfts": [0.709359, 0.729975, 4.277035]
}
```

This E2E run covers the Python client and `/v1/completions` endpoint.
Chat Completions and Rust behavior are covered by the targeted tests above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Capture CUDA graphs with expandable segments off for AITER all-reduce
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `expandable_segments:True`, the caching allocator hands out VMM-backed pointers, which `hipIpcGetMemHandle` cannot export. AITER's custom all-reduce therefore stages every all-reduce captured in a CUDA graph through a device-to-device copy.

The activations feeding those all-reduces are allocated inside graph capture from the graph's private pool. Turning expandable segments off for the duration of `graph_capture()` makes them exportable, so AITER takes its registered, copy-free path. Weights, KV cache and allocations made outside `graph_capture()` keep expandable segments.

No flag. It applies automatically on ROCm when the TP group's AITER custom all-reduce registers graph buffers (`AiterCustomAllreduce.registers_graph_buffers`). That needs vLLM not to have turned registration off (the cuMem graph pool), the communicator to be enabled, a non-gfx1250 GPU, and AITER's public `defers_capture_registration` class marker. The marker means AITER takes the registration decision when capture begins; it was added in ROCm/aiter#5799 and first released in v0.1.26.

It is skipped when the DP group also runs AITER collectives. Under DP+EP the MoE combine reduce-scatters a persistent workspace allocated before capture, which the registered path cannot export.

Nothing changes on AITER before v0.1.26 (vLLM pins v0.1.26 since #62486), without AITER custom all-reduce, with the cuMem graph pool, on gfx1250, or when expandable segments are already off.

`non_expandable_allocations()` (`vllm/device_allocator/alloc_conf.py`) flips only that field of the live allocator config and restores the full string on exit, including on error. It uses the same read/flip/restore pattern as `CuMemAllocator.use_memory_pool`.

## Test Plan

- `pytest -v -s tests/device_allocator`
- `pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_rocm_aiter_custom_ar.py` (2 GPUs; runs in the existing AMD CI step)
- Before/after kernel trace: rocprofv3 `--kernel-trace` on Qwen3-0.6B TP2 decode with cudagraphs, per decode graph replay per rank.
- MI355X, image `nightly-rocm100-77154ca6` with this PR's `vllm/` diff applied. AITER is either v0.1.25 + the ROCm/aiter#5799 diff (Python-only; real v0.1.26 adds only gfx1250 symm_mem and `gemma_norm`, the capture path is identical) or stock v0.1.25. All runs use `PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` unless noted.
  - Gate: Qwen3-0.6B(-FP8, `fuse_allreduce_rms`) at TP1 and TP2, with AITER custom AR on and off, and with expandable segments off.
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP8 (no mono decode, DSpark k=6 synthetic AL 3.87) with and without SWA bounded replay. Decode benchmark: random 1024 in / 256 out at concurrency 1 and 8.

## Test Result

- `tests/device_allocator`: 31 passed (30 on main).
- `tests/distributed/test_rocm_aiter_custom_ar.py` on MI355X:

  - `test_rocm_aiter_custom_allreduce_skips_copy_with_expandable_segments` runs on 2 GPUs. It turns `expandable_segments` on, then asserts that inside `graph_capture()` AITER takes the registered path (input bound directly, no staging copy). It also checks the all-reduce result after replay and that expandable segments are restored.
  - Results: all pass with #5799. With the guard forced off, the second test fails. On AITER without #5799, the marker test fails and the GPU test is skipped.
- Before/after trace (Qwen3-0.6B TP2, `expandable_segments:True`; "before" is AITER v0.1.25 = copy-in), per decode graph replay per rank. The counts are identical on both ranks and over all 63 decode steps:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| AITER all-reduce kernels | 57 | 57 |
| `__amd_rocclr_copyBuffer` (staging copy) | 58 | 1 |
| copyBuffer immediately before an all-reduce | 57 | 0 |
| kernels in the replay | 396 | 339 |

  The one remaining copyBuffer is the FULL graph's output copy. Greedy outputs are identical. Unprofiled decode step: 1.29 → 1.20 ms at batch 1 (−7%) and 1.46 → 1.35 ms at batch 4 (−8%). The raw traces are attached in the review thread.
- Gate behaviour:

| Config | Guard | AITER capture path |
|---|---|---|
| TP2, AITER with #5799 | on | registered on every rank |
| TP2, AITER with #5799, expandable off | on (no-op) | registered |
| TP2, stock AITER v0.1.25 | off | copy-in |
| TP1 | off | no AITER all-reduce |
| TP2, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0` | off | vLLM's own custom all-reduce, which fails under expandable segments with or without this PR |

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP8 with expandable segments on, measured over one serving run per arm:
  - With SWA bounded replay on, every rank takes the registered path, including in the decoder-replay graphs: 48 lines across 8 ranks, no errors.
  - Decode step vs copy-in (stock v0.1.25): -2.9% at c1 (8.79 vs 9.05 ms) and -1.5% at c8 (11.72 vs 11.90 ms).
  - With replay off, two runs per arm: -2.6% at c1 and -2.0% at c8. That matches running with expandable segments off.
  - Cost: graph pool +0.4-0.5 GiB per GPU, the same as with expandable segments off. KV cache -0.2% (-0.26% with replay on).
- Kimi-K3 8x MI355X MTP K=4 (earlier revision, same mechanism), TPOT P50 at 8k c1 / 8k c8:

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Fix HTTP 500 from max_tokens_per_doc when the query…
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**TL;DR:** On BERT-style cross-encoders, `/rerank`, `/score` and `LLM.score` return HTTP 500 when `max_tokens_per_doc` is set and the query alone fills the token limit. This falls back to the usual truncation in that case.

No existing issue or PR covers this. #60877 edits the same file but not this code.

## Claims

These requests no longer fail with HTTP 500:
- `truncate_prompt_tokens` below the query length plus special tokens, with or without an empty document. They now get the usual truncation, as without `max_tokens_per_doc`.
- A query longer than `max_model_len` without truncation. It now gets the usual 400 "maximum context length" error.

Requests that work today produce the same tokens.

## Validation

`vllm serve cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2` on a T4. The query is a passage (as in "find similar"), with `max_tokens_per_doc=8`:

| Request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `truncate_prompt_tokens=16` | 500 | 200 |
| same, plus an empty document | 500 | 200 |
| 600-token query, no truncation | 500 | 400 "maximum context length" |

On main all three fail with `Truncation error: Sequence to truncate too short to respect the provided max_length`. With the fix, the relevant document still ranks first.

Tests, main → this PR:
- `tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py`: 10 → 14 passed. The 4 new tests are listed below; 3 of them fail on main.
- `test_cross_encoder_online.py` 20/20, `test_cross_encoder_offline.py` 6/6, `tests/models/language/pooling/test_max_tokens_per_doc.py` 20/20, on both.

Also compared the preprocessing on main and this branch over 18,360 combinations of query and document length and both limits. Only the 2,250 that failed on main changed, and none of them goes over either limit.

## Details

**Root cause.** With `max_tokens_per_doc`, `get_score_prompt` encodes the pair with `truncation="only_second"`. That can only shorten the document, so the tokenizer raises when query + special tokens already reach `max_length`.

**Fix.** Use `only_second` only when the query leaves room for at least one document token. Otherwise the existing `truncation=True` arguments apply. The document is already cut to `max_tokens_per_doc` as text before encoding, so that limit still holds.

**Trade-off.** In the fallback the query is shortened. This can't be avoided when the query alone fills the limit, and it's what `truncate_prompt_tokens` already does without a document limit.

**New tests**, using a toy BERT-style tokenizer:
- When the query fits, only the document is cut. This passes on main too.
- When the query fills the limit, the usual truncation applies, for a normal and an empty document.
- A query that is too long without truncation gets the usual validation error.

commits.pr_title: [Model][Perf] Fuse Beam's TP all-reduce with its sandwich norms and MoE finalize
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fuse Beam's TP all-reduce with its sandwich norms and, for TRTLLM-Gen NvFP4 MoE layers, the top-k finalize. TP only; replicated-token EP deferral is in #62073, which builds on this PR. Follow-up to #62074 (merged). The kernel is built ahead of time in `csrc/beam/`, with no runtime JIT and no CUDA source in the model folder.

## Claims

- `csrc/beam/allreduce_norm.cu`: MNNVL one-shot/two-shot all-reduce with Beam's FP32 norm-residual-norm epilogue and an optional MoE finalize before the reduction (keeping the local BF16 rounding). Exposed as `torch.ops._C.beam_allreduce_norm`, plus `beam_allreduce` (two-shot all-reduce only) for the large-batch path, which then runs the Triton boundary kernel.
- `csrc/mnnvl_lamport.cuh`: the subset of FlashInfer's MNNVL Lamport device helpers (`trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh`, v0.7.2, the version vLLM pins) that the kernel uses, vendored with its license header.
- Beam defers the TRTLLM-Gen NvFP4 top-k finalize into the fused all-reduce under TP, using the existing `FusedMoEConfig.defer_moe_finalize()`. No shared MoE code changes.
- Same speed as the previous JIT build of this kernel, and 6–16% faster at hidden 8192 from 64 tokens up (microbenchmarks below).

## Validation

**Unit tests** on GB200 (4 GPUs):

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_beam_construction.py tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py
```

178 passed, 3 skipped (8-GPU case; two upstream FlashInfer tile-config skips). This covers the 2- and 4-rank all-reduce and MoE finalize numerics.

**TP8 across two GB200 nodes** (one MNNVL clique): the all-reduce numerics worker from `test_beam_numerics.py` (batch changes, one-shot/two-shot, large-batch path, CUDA-graph replay) passes at hidden 5120 and 8192 when launched with `torchrun --nnodes=2`. The 8-rank MoE-finalize case was not run (its test is single-node).

**FlashInfer version:** these runs used an environment with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 installed. `trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh` is byte-identical in v0.7.2, and the `flashinfer.comm.mnnvl` allocator APIs used here are unchanged (v0.7.2 only adds NVML init/shutdown around a capability probe).

**Build:** `_C_stable_libtorch` built for SM100 with CUDA 13.2; `csrc/beam/allreduce_norm.cu` also compiles for `sm_90a`. Not run on Hopper.

**Kernel microbenchmark**, GB200, BF16, each op captured 20× in a CUDA graph; µs per call, slowest rank. "JIT" is the previous FlashInfer-JIT build of the same kernel, "AOT" is this one. Fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm:

| config | 1 tok | 8 tok | 64 tok | 256 tok | 1024 tok | 4096 tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4, hidden 5120 (JIT → AOT) | 5.39 → 5.75* | 5.48 → 5.43 | 8.70 → 8.78 | 11.71 → 11.67 | 34.06 → 33.71 | 138.0 → 139.2 |
| TP4, hidden 8192 | 6.34 → 6.31 | 6.34 → 6.21 | 9.97 → 9.34 | 19.00 → 16.05 | 64.52 → 54.28 | 251.2 → 226.8 |
| TP8, hidden 5120 | 6.53 → 6.48 | 6.42 → 6.39 | 9.00 → 8.97 | 12.89 → 12.88 | 35.52 → 35.53 | 140.3 → 140.4 |
| TP8, hidden 8192 | 7.86 → 7.78 | 7.98 → 7.91 | 10.59 → 9.88 | 19.82 → 16.67 | 68.27 → 57.19 | 265.1 → 225.8 |

TP4 is the median of 3 runs; TP8 is the mean of two runs with the measurement order swapped. \*Whichever kernel is measured first in a process reads about 0.4 µs slow at 1 token; with the order reversed, TP4/5120 at 1 token is 5.79 (JIT) → 5.36 (AOT). The kernel code is unchanged: register usage matches, and at hidden 5120 the AOT kernel on the JIT path's workspace matches the JIT kernel within 0.07 µs. The hidden-8192 gap appears only with the JIT path's own workspace sized for 8192 tokens (it vanishes at 4096); its cause was not isolated.

**Performance:** TODO — end-to-end before/after against #62074 (standard TP all-reduce), TP8 batch-1 decode and 8 × 2K prefill on GB200.

## Details

- **Why vendor FlashInfer's helpers instead of reusing vLLM's MNNVL Lamport kernels:** on GB200, vLLM's Lamport all-gather (`csrc/custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.cuh`) is about 10% slower at TP4 and 25–40% slower at TP8 than FlashInfer's one-shot all-reduce, which does the same communication plus a reduction (TP8, 64 tokens × 5120: 16.7 vs 11.9 µs). Its reduce-scatter + all-gather pair is 1.3–1.8× slower than FlashInfer's single-launch two-shot. A likely cause is that vLLM waits on peer ranks one at a time, while FlashInfer polls them all at once; not verified with a patched kernel. Building on vLLM's primitives would have regressed Beam, so the device code is kept as-is.
- **Workspace:** FlashInfer's `McastGPUBuffer` still maps the multicast memory. The Lamport protocol, its initialization and its generation flags are vLLM's, so the build no longer depends on FlashInfer's headers or installed version. Torch symmetric memory works too, but measured 0.2–0.3 µs slower per call at 1–4 tokens (even from 8 tokens up). Rounding it to the 512 MB multicast granularity didn't help. Beam's GB200 path already requires FlashInfer for its MoE.
- **Build:** compiled only for SM90/SM100 (`VLLM_ENABLE_BEAM_ALLREDUCE`), with `--fmad=false` on that file only, so the FP32 boundary math is not contracted into FMAs. `BeamAllReduceWorkspace.create` returns `None` (standard TP all-reduce) when the op is not built, multicast is unavailable on any rank, or the shape/TP size is unsupported.
- **CI coverage:** `tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py` runs on a CPU agent in Buildkite, so the GPU and multi-GPU cases skip in CI. They were run on GB200 as above.
- **Scope:** an earlier revision also added `defer_moe_finalize(allow_ep=True)` to `FusedMoEConfig` for TP=1, EP>1. It moved to #62073, which extends it to MegaMoE under DP/EP, so this PR leaves the shared MoE config untouched.
- **Not a duplicate:** no other open PR touches Beam's all-reduce.

## Summary

Follow-up to #59332, which cut these tests to keep that PR scoped to what
#54966 ("Test padding") originally asked for. Tracked in the progress table
at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54966#issuecomment-6129972192
(item 4, follow-up row) as "4d-1".

Adds three tests to `tests/rocm/test_moe_padding.py`, extending the existing
`_maybe_pad_weight` coverage:

- `test_maybe_pad_weight_eplb_disables_padding` -- EPLB requires contiguous
  weights for its rearrangement ops, so padding must stay off whenever EPLB
  is enabled, even for an otherwise-eligible (512-byte-aligned) shape.
- `test_maybe_pad_weight_non_unit_stride_disables_padding` -- `_maybe_pad_weight`
  requires a unit inner stride; constructs a strided view whose *would-be*
  outer-stride alignment passes, to prove the stride guard specifically (not
  just alignment) is what blocks padding.
- `test_aiter_moe_padding_rl_reload_address_stable` -- simulates an RL
  in-place weight reload (same `RoutedExperts` layer, new weight values) and
  asserts `w13_weight`/`w2_weight`'s storage address is unchanged across the
  reload, confirming `process_weights_after_loading` copies the padded
  weight back into existing storage rather than rebinding `.data` (which
  would silently break CUDA-graph address capture). Also checks the
  post-reload output reflects the new weights.

## Test plan

Ran on an MI355X (gfx950) host, AITER v0.1.26:

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -v -s tests/rocm/test_moe_padding.py
```

All 10 tests in the file (7 existing + 3 new) pass. `pre-commit run --files
tests/rocm/test_moe_padding.py` is clean.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Align CPU offload pool size across PP/spec-decode workers
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix CPU offload block-count mismatches between the scheduler and workers under uneven pipeline parallelism or speculative decoding, preventing out-of-bounds offload copies.

## Claims

- Workers synchronize the block count with MIN before allocating offload storage.
- The engine queries the aligned count only for enabled `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` configurations, including `MultiConnector`, and requires a valid worker result.
- The scheduler uses that count directly. Removed the unused config-based fallback and per-worker config plumbing.

## Validation

After merging main (`f143f65d7c74`) and cherry-picking the Nixl CI fix, Python 3.12 / CPU:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/config/test_config_utils.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py -q
```

- **144 passed, 18 skipped**. The CPU-offload worker module and 17 GPU-dependent embed-sharing cases require CUDA/ROCm and were skipped; this includes the three worker synchronization tests. The failing AMD GPU cases must be validated in CI.
- Six focused regression cases cover RPC gating, MultiConnector and a missing worker result. The missing-result case failed before the assertion was added and now passes.
- `bash -n tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh` and pre-commit checks on all PR files passed, including shellcheck, Ruff and mypy. Inapplicable actionlint was excluded because its Go download failed certificate validation; no workflow files changed.

Previously reported ROCm smoke validation, before these review fixes:

| Configuration | Baseline worker / scheduler blocks | Aligned blocks | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kimi-K3 TP4×PP2 | Workers 50 / 46; scheduler 50 | 46 everywhere | Two-pass generation matched |
| Kimi-K3 TP8×PP2, two-node MI355X | Workers 809 / 746; scheduler 809 | 746 everywhere | Health and completion smoke passed |

These runs used dummy weights and `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5a4c8d99242e9e069b604d0e9b969e77f7dd501d`. GPU/PP smoke tests were not rerun for the current review fixes on this CPU-only host.

## Details

CI dependencies: merged main to include the AMD fixture fix in [#62869](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62869). Also cherry-picked only [`4ca9ef5ded05`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/4ca9ef5ded05b393c6a6978574dba4598a2dd543) from the still-open [#62879](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62879), preserving its author and provenance. Its 11-line test-script change waits for prefillers to be ready before starting decoders that share their GPUs, preventing overlapping memory profiling and weight loading. This addresses a Nixl CI failure also observed on main; GPU validation is pending CI. The dependency is already proposed upstream rather than being a separate new fix PR here.

Heavier PP ranks can store fewer blocks in the same byte budget, while the scheduler previously sized its pool using a lighter rank. The resulting block IDs could exceed a worker's allocation and crash a copy operation.

Workers derive capacity from live KV storage; the startup RPC transfers the aligned result to the scheduler. With offloading enabled, a missing result is an initialization error rather than a reason to estimate capacity again. The explicit `num_cpu_blocks` override remains supported.

This provides automatic alignment rather than requiring per-topology tuning such as InferenceX's `KV_OFFLOAD_MAX_CPU_BLOCKS` workaround. Open PRs were searched for matching SimpleCPUOffload/PP alignment work at initial submission; none matched this automatic fix.

AI assistance: Cursor for the original implementation and Codex for these review fixes.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash specialized decode on GB300
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR adds an NVIDIA specialized decode for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300, for the small decode batches that agentic serving runs. It supports:
- one GB300 tray at TP4;
- DSpark speculative decoding with 5 draft tokens;
- FULL-graph decode steps of up to 384 rows (64 requests × 6 tokens). Prefill, mixed batches and larger batches fall back to the stock forward.

It is opt-in via `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`, the same switch as #61867. With the default (`auto`), the model runs exactly as on upstream `main`. The model changes are all under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`; outside it, the PR only adds tests and a CI step.

The integration follows #61867: the model owns a decode executor that takes over FULL-graph decode steps. The stacked follow-up #61869 puts the DSpark draft model on the same executor. Both follow the RFC #59665 fast-track process. Related: #57448 (DeepSeek-V4.1 tracking), #59725 (Cake kernels).

## Claims

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray with DSpark, the same build with the switch on and off:
- Decode step (one speculative step, including the draft): **18.3% faster at batch 1** (5,355 → 4,375 µs), 13.7% at batch 8 and 11.3% at batch 32.
- InferenceX AgentX traces: **P90 interactivity up 16–24%** at every concurrency from 1 to 64, with throughput per GPU up 1–6% and TTFT unchanged.
- GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond, AIME25 and RULER NIAH stay within one point of the switch-off model, and the DSpark acceptance length does not change.

## Validation

### Correctness

The reference is the same build with the switch off. GPQA-Diamond and AIME25 use reasoning effort high and temperature 0.6.

| Task | Samples | Switch off | Switch on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K, strict match (c1 / c8 / c32) | 1,319 per cell | 0.973 / 0.972 / 0.973 | 0.974 / 0.970 / 0.975 |
| GPQA-Diamond | 198 × 16 | 0.796 | 0.788 |
| AIME25 | 30 × 16 | 0.994 | 0.990 |
| RULER NIAH single / multikey-2 / multikey-3, 32K / 128K / 256K (c1 and c8) | | 1.0 in every cell | 1.0 in every cell |
| DSpark acceptance length on GSM8K (c1 / c8 / c32) | | 3.93 / 3.95 / 3.93 | 3.93 / 3.96 / 3.97 |

- **GPQA-Diamond.** Paired by question over the 16 repeats, on − off is −0.79 ± 0.56 points (bootstrap 95% interval −2.2 to +0.6). The first eight repeats gave −1.6 points, mostly answers that ran past the 16,384-token limit without a final answer; the second eight gave +0.06.
- **Later revisions.** GSM8K at c8 was rerun after each later change, with its mean acceptance length: 0.972 and 3.92 on `main` `429a3da` (FlashInfer 0.7.1), 0.975 and 3.95 on `011fa68c`, 0.971 and 3.97 after the move into the executor, 0.976 and 3.96 with the CuTe DSL kernels, 0.972 and 3.99 after the rebase onto `main` `03ee2e13` (FlashInfer 0.7.2), 0.975 and 3.92 after the rebase onto `main` `aa3564ce`, and 0.972 and 3.91 after the rebase onto `main` `3b518982`. Both rebases also changed compiled code in `main` (the first DeepGEMM's build and the top-k kernels, the second the top-k softmax and DCP kernels), so the decode step was timed across each on one GB300 tray (old `main` wheel and branch against new, blocks old-new-new-old, two repeats each): B1 +0.1%, B8 +0.8%, B32 +0.4% across the first, and B1 −0.2%, B8 −0.1%, B32 −0.1% across the second, all within noise (|t| < 2), so the performance numbers in this description still stand. After each rebase the kernel, numerics and layers tests pass again (run at the tip of #61869, which contains this PR).

The tests check each kernel against the stock op it replaces, the TP4 collectives bitwise against the unfused path, and a five-layer model served with the switch on and off:

<details><summary>Tests, sanitizers and CI</summary>

```bash
# One SM100-family GPU: each kernel against the stock op it replaces
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py -v
# Four GPUs: TP4 collectives bitwise against the unfused reference, and graph replays
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_numerics.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_numerics --replays 100000  # race stress
# Four GB300: five-layer model on random weights at TP4 with DSpark, switch on vs off
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_layers.py -v
```

| Check | What it covers | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kernel tests | Each kernel against the stock op it replaces, at every supported row count, eagerly and replayed from a CUDA graph | 90 passed |
| Numerics (TP4) | The fused collectives bitwise against the unfused reference over 1,000 graph replays; the indexer top-k equal up to boundary ties | Passed |
| Race stress | 100,000 graph replays: collectives bitwise, top-k sets equal throughout | Passed before the restructure, which changed no kernel |
| Layers test (4× GB300) | A five-layer model at TP4 with DSpark, served with the switch on and off; the activations of every layer are compared within tolerance. The test checks which paths each layer took, that the executor ran on the switch-on steps and that it never ran with the switch off | Passed |
| compute-sanitizer (CUDA 13.0.2) over the kernel tests | memcheck, synccheck, racecheck | memcheck: no errors. synccheck: no report in this PR's kernels. Kernels that are not this PR's are left uninstrumented, because synccheck aborts every kernel it reports: FlashInfer's TRT-LLM-gen kernels and CuTe DSL dense GEMMs, and vLLM's `LLBf16SplitK`, which this PR calls ("Divergent thread(s) in block"). racecheck: FlashInfer's CuTe DSL split-K `mm_bf16`, which the LM head calls, reports shared-memory hazards; upstream calls the same kernel from its BF16 linear backend. No other test reports a hazard: cooperative top-k, the sparse-MLA KV counters, the MXFP8 projections, the index key store, Engram, the side-stream table builds and the metadata graphs are racecheck-clean. Those were run over the DSpark PR's kernel tests, which include all of this PR's, before the restructure, which changed none of them. The CuTe DSL routed-expert kernels were checked with all three tools at this revision: no memcheck error, no synccheck report and no race hazard. |
| pre-commit | All hooks | Passes on every changed file |

**CI.** A new 4×B200 step runs the kernel, numerics and layers tests. Like the other 4×B200 steps, it is optional, so it runs nightly rather than on every PR. No CI agent has four GB300, so the layers test skips there; it and the end-to-end results were run on GB300 outside CI.

</details>

### Performance

All runs use DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4) with DSpark (5 draft tokens), Model Runner V2 and FULL CUDA graphs for decode. The switch-off arm is upstream `main` at the same base.
